    This Oceanfront Hilton Resort in Florida Is Great for Groups

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1477 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nerdwallet

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Hilton is making a major play in South Florida with its Signia by Hilton Diplomat Beach Resort.
    • The resort caters primarily to business and group travelers (it’s attached to a massive events space), but it’s also a strong option for vacationers looking for some R&R.
    • According to recent reports, room rates typically run $300 to $600 a night, depending on the season, but you can also use Hilton Honors benefits to make your stay more affordable.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Hilton is making a major play in South Florida with its Signia by Hilton Diplomat Beach Resort. The massive 1,000-room property — which underwent an $80 million renovation before opening under the Signia Hilton brand in May 2026 — sits on the beach in Hollywood, Florida, just outside of Fort Lauderdale.

    The resort caters primarily to business and group travelers (it’s attached to a massive events space), but it’s also a strong option for vacationers looking for some R&R. The main downside: The location isn’t great if your trip primarily revolves around off-property excursions, dining and nightlife.

    According to recent reports, room rates typically run $300 to $600 a night, depending on the season, but you can also use Hilton Honors benefits to make your stay more affordable. There’s also a resort fee of $59 per night — but Hilton waives that when you book using Hilton points.

    Hilton covered the cost of my stay for two nights, but the opinions in this review are my own. Here’s what guests can expect at this oceanfront resort.

    Since the Signia by Hilton Diplomat Beach Resort is part of Hilton Honors, there are several ways to book a stay there.

    If you’re using Hilton points, expect to pay 70,000 to 80,000 points a night when standard rooms are available. Hilton elite status — a benefit you can earn by holding any Hilton Honors credit card — gets you the fifth-night-free perk, where you stay for at least five nights but pay for four when booking with points.

    For example, if you were to stay five nights at 80,000 points a night, you’d pay 320,000 points total, bringing down your average nightly rate to 64,000 points.

    You can also book using Hilton’s generous free night certificates, which can be used at almost any property in the portfolio. If you hold the Hilton Honors American Express Aspire Card, you automatically get a certificate each year. It’s also possible to earn certificates through reaching spending thresholds on the card and on the Hilton Honors American Express Surpass® Card. Terms apply.

    It has been revealed that make sure to check the cash rate against the points rate to make sure you’re getting good value from your redemption. NerdWallet values Hilton points at 0.4 cent apiece.

    For cash bookings of two nights or more, you might consider using The Hotel Collection via American Express’ travel portal for eligible cardholders. Eligible bookings come with benefits like a $100 property credit and other amenities subject to availability, including a room upgrade, early check-in and late checkout.

    Keep in mind that third-party bookings typically don’t earn Hilton points or count toward elite status qualification.

    It’s hard to miss the Signia by Hilton Diplomat Beach Resort, with its signature H-shaped facade and sleek white-and-glass exterior.

    According to recent reports, stepping into the hotel, I was immediately struck by the lush greenery filling the entrance and indoor courtyard. The grand lobby has soaring glass ceilings, giving the space a greenhouse feel, although the strong air conditioning keeps you cool.

    Despite its massive size, it doesn’t have a sprawling layout, which I appreciated. Everything is close together, and you can walk from the check-in counter to any of the indoor restaurants in under a minute.

    Industry observers note that I stayed in an oceanfront suite with a balcony, which was spacious and had a fun beachy vibe. To get to the rooms, you’ll need to use either the north or south tower elevator banks.

    In the living room, there was a large sitting area featuring a TV, a couch, an accent chair and a four-person high-top table.

    Although I didn’t spend too much time on the balcony — the October balminess was a bit too much for me — I enjoyed stepping out each morning to admire the view.

    The bedroom had a king bed with extremely comfortable bedding and an oversized chair that was a great spot to relax and read a book by the window.

    The bathroom was spacious, featuring a shower and a separate tub (something every room has).

    According to recent reports, even the standard room I toured felt roomy. I liked that it shared similar elements with the suite, including the oversized lounge chair.

    This is what you’d normally get when booking a room at the cheapest points price.

    There are several dining venues on the property, ranging from a grab-and-go cafe to a high-end steakhouse. It is a luxury resort, so expect the prices to reflect that.

    For breakfast, you can head to Palmea Kitchen, which is also open for lunch. I had the breakfast buffet, which offered a nice spread of classics, from hot food items and pastries to cold cuts and smoked salmon.

    According to recent reports, if you don’t have time for a sit-down breakfast, you can head next door to The Press, which offers made-to-order and grab-and-go food options throughout the day. You can also get smoothies, juices, snacks, pastries and other sweet treats.

    The Canteen is another grab-and-go option that also sells snacks, drinks, souvenirs and sundries, similar to a convenience store.

    For lunch and dinner, try Solara. It doesn’t have a traditional restaurant feel, as it’s mostly an indoor-outdoor bar space. One side connects to the lobby, while the other side faces the Solara adults-only pool.

    It serves a lunch menu, as well as a substantial bar food menu that’s available late into the night.

    Recent findings suggest that you can also eat at Playa Beach Bar & Grill, a beachside restaurant serving Latin-inspired cuisine. I enjoyed spending a lazy lunch there and watching the waves crash onto the shore.

    For a fancy sit-down dinner, go to Diplomat Prime, the property’s steakhouse. We had a group dinner at the restaurant, and the meats were, of course, the highlight. But don’t sleep on the seafood, which was also delicious.

    One of the best parts of the Dip, as it’s affectionately known, is its location right on the beach. Guests can access the stretch of beach directly adjacent to the property. But it’s not a private beach, so you might encounter crowds.

    I didn’t spend any time on the beach itself — it was extremely windy while I was there — but the hotel’s resort fee includes amenities like a beach lounge (umbrella not included), a daily one-hour kayak or paddleboard rental, and beachfront yoga classes.

    If you don’t want to get sand everywhere, you can head to one of the three pool options: the adults-only Solara pool, the family-friendly lagoon pool and the Verandah Social Club for those 21 and older (requires paid access).

    Recent findings suggest that the family-friendly lagoon spans the length of the property and runs beneath the Solara pool. It also has its own hot tub.

    I spent an afternoon in a cabana at the Verandah Social Club, which has some smaller plunge pools and a hot tub.

    I appreciated the attentive service from the staff there, who constantly checked on whether guests needed anything.

    If you’re looking for other ways to stay active, head to the two-story fitness center, featuring a variety of equipment like free weights, exercise bikes, a rowing machine and treadmills.

    Next door, you’ll find the spa and wellness center. I had a relaxing massage that incorporated hot stones and aromatherapy.

    The locker rooms come with a sauna and steam room, although I wished there were more amenities like a hot tub and cold plunge.

    In a recent development, one of the resort fee inclusions is complimentary high-intensity interval training workout classes at the gym across the street. I signed up for an early morning class. The instructor was friendly, and it was a great way to start my day.

    Other amenities include a complimentary one-hour e-bike rental each day, as well as a kids’ club with various activities (but drop-off fees apply).

    I had a fantastic stay at this resort, but I’d recommend it for a specific traveler.

    If you’re planning to stay on-property your entire trip, it’s a great option. That’s probably why it’s such a popular convention hotel, since everything you need is easily accessible.

    I loved the hotel’s design, including the jungle-like atmosphere in the lobby, and I found the dining options to be tasty, albeit pricey.

    But if your trip revolves around visiting Miami attractions, you’ll likely want to stay closer to the action.

    #142357. Are Employees Using Firm AI To Hunt For Other Jobs​?

    📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (922 w)
    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Forbes ↗ Open Full Page

    Are Employees Using Firm AI To Hunt For Other Jobs​?

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (922 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Forbes

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Ken Ringdahl is the Chief Technology Officer at Emburse.
    • Sources indicate that even as enterprises say farewell to “tokenmaxxing” and hello to “tokenminning” to rein in ballooning AI costs, some employees are still using AI for everything they can.
    • My company’s June study on expense fraud found that 61% of U.S.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Ken Ringdahl is the Chief Technology Officer at Emburse.

    Sources indicate that even as enterprises say farewell to “tokenmaxxing” and hello to “tokenminning” to rein in ballooning AI costs, some employees are still using AI for everything they can. That “everything” includes a healthy share of non-work-related tasks.​.

    My company’s June study on expense fraud found that 61% of U.S. and U.K. business professionals use employer-funded AI tools for personal purposes. Another survey from research institute Epoch AI found that 76% of responding employees with employer-provided AI subscriptions “reported using AI at least as much for work as for personal tasks.”.

    Recent findings suggest that while enterprises limit agentic coding tools to cut down on AI spending, workers are using those same licenses to fix their dating profiles, initiative weddings and write cover letters. If that’s not a sign to get serious about implementing AI spend control and usage policies, I don’t know what is.

    Recent findings suggest that according to our survey, 26% of responding U.S. and U.K. professionals admitted that nearly a third of their logged AI use was for personal reasons. These ranged from routine tasks to major life events, such as:​.

    • Handling life admin, such as meal planning or gift research (23%).

    • Asking for life and relationship advice (17%).

    • Planning a wedding or other special event (13%).

    • Improving a dating profile (8%)​.

    It has been revealed that asking AI to draft a cover letter or a meal plan doesn’t burn tokens at nearly the same rate as legitimate enterprise use cases such as writing code or multistep reasoning, for example. Still, these costs add up, particularly when personal queries account for a meaningful portion of overall AI use. Enterprises are scrambling to control AI costs while unwittingly financing employees’ job searches.

    Ask if they’d consider their activity to be misuse, and many employees would point out that they’ve been encouraged or even pressured to adopt these tools. In fact, some think crossing the line between home and work benefits their employers.

    The number one reason (stated by 35% of U.S. employees we surveyed) workers are motivated to use their employers’ AI tools is to be more effective in their personal lives so they can ultimately be more effective on the job. Another 25% mentioned that employer-sponsored programs either mandating or promoting AI drive them to use these tools outside of work to “learn faster.”.

    Further underscoring the need for education and clearer guidelines, we found that 23% of respondents noted they simply weren’t aware of policies against personal AI usage.

    It has been revealed that businesses depend on their employees to become AI-proficient. They need to make the most of their investments. How can they keep workers safe and compliant once they’ve handed over the keys to the toolshed?​.

    Stronger infosec controls have to be part of the solution. HERE Enterprise’s August 2026 “AI Toggle Tax Survey” found that 72% of enterprise workers admitted to navigating around their organization’s AI policies. Popular workarounds included using personal AI accounts on company-issued devices or using corporate AI tools on their personal devices.

    Recent findings suggest that secure web gateways (SWG) can help prevent this by blocking unauthorized LLM access. Data loss prevention (DLP) tools can reduce the risk of sensitive data leaks. Browser-level controls can redact or watermark an AI-assisted export before it leaves the workspace and prevent capture when PII is displayed on screen.​.

    Education is another part. Because many AI tools are presented as chat interfaces, employees can forget they’re sharing information with an outside provider. Employees may not realize that inputting something as “harmless” as a spreadsheet of wedding guest contact information risks exposing personal data.

    It has been revealed that crafting an AI usage policy can unite both of these efforts, and every credible one starts with a list of approved tools. InfoSec, finance and IT should work with procurement to vet AI vendors and publish a record of which platforms are cleared for what tasks and with what data. Anything off-list should be off-limits by default. This group should scrub the list on a quarterly basis, since latest enterprise tools pop up every day. ​.

    It has been revealed that your AI usage policy should also make it clear what data can and can’t leave the perimeter. Describe your infosec controls in plain language so employees think twice about taking their work AI tools home with them.​.

    If companies knew more about how employees were using their AI, they’d cut a lot of waste and reinvest in revenue-driving activities. Finance already tracks spend by vendor and department everywhere else in the business. Why shouldn’t AI platforms get the same treatment?

    In a recent development, the problem is that treating employees like suspects as you investigate their AI use hardly fosters an innovation culture. A better approach is to ask teams to make the business case for the tools they want. At my company, teams requesting a new AI platform are required to state the expected return as part of our review process. Once approved, we evaluate its impact at regular intervals. That encourages a sense of ownership.​.

    When teams are responsible for proving ROI, they’re more likely to use AI tools judiciously. You don’t want to police every prompt. You do want to make AI spend, access and accountability as disciplined as every other business investment.​.

    In a recent development, forbes Technology Council is an invitation-only community for world-class CIOs, CTOs and technology executives. Do I qualify?

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Atmos Rewards is the airline loyalty program for Alaska Airlines and Hawaiian Airlines.
    • There are six communities, including two reserved for Alaska and Hawaii residents.
    • Here’s how to decide which Atmos Community best fits your travel patterns.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Atmos Rewards is the airline loyalty program for Alaska Airlines and Hawaiian Airlines. One of its newer features is Atmos Communities, which offer additional rewards and benefits tailored to different travel interests.

    There are six communities, including two reserved for Alaska and Hawaii residents. The other four are open to members regardless of where they live. But don’t get caught up in the community names. The best choice for you may depend more on your travel looks than the groupings suggest.

    Here’s how to decide which Atmos Community best fits your travel patterns.

    » Learn more: The guide to Atmos Rewards.

    Atmos Communities are like groups within the Atmos Rewards program that offer additional benefits based on different travel interests.

    Sources indicate that they’re free to join for Atmos Rewards members. Four communities are available to all members, while community Club 49 is reserved for Alaska residents and community Huaka’i by Hawaiian is reserved for Hawaii residents.

    Industry observers note that you can belong to only one community at a time and switch communities once per calendar year. Consider your upcoming travel plans before choosing.

    Sources indicate that each Atmos Community has a list of 10 destinations where members can earn bonus points and status points. Although the destinations differ by community, the rewards structure is the same.

    It has been revealed that through Dec. 31, 2027, members can earn up to 10,000 bonus points and 10,000 status points by visiting qualifying destinations.

    Here’s how many points you’ll earn as you reach each milestone:.

    Visit one destination, earn 100 status and bonus points.

    Visit two destinations, earn 200 status and bonus points.

    Visit three destinations, earn 300 status and bonus points.

    Visit four destinations, earn 400 status and bonus points.

    Visit five destinations, earn 500 status and bonus points.

    Visit six destinations, earn 750 status and bonus points.

    Visit seven destinations, earn 1,000 status and bonus points.

    Visit eight destinations, earn 1,250 status and bonus points.

    Visit nine destinations, earn 2,500 status and bonus points.

    Visit 10 destinations, earn 3,000 status and bonus points.

    The first member of each community to visit all 10 qualifying destinations during the challenge period will also earn 100,000 bonus points.

    According to recent reports, upcoming lists of qualifying destinations for each community take effect on Jan. 1, 2028.

    Here’s a closer look at the six communities, their benefits and the destinations eligible for bonus points.

    Global Locals is geared toward frequent international travelers. Benefits include:.

    Earn 10% more status points toward Atmos elite status on flights that begin and/or end outside the U.S., including award flights.

    #142352. Latest Update: The AI Gateway Is Becoming The Enterprise Control Point

    📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (926 w)
    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech 📈 Bullish 🌐 Forbes ↗ Open Full Page

    Latest Update: The AI Gateway Is Becoming The Enterprise Control Point

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (926 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Forbes

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Joan Vendrell, NeuralTrust CEO and cofounder, has 15+ years of technology leadership experience advancing enterprise-grade AI security.
    • ​In 2025, attackers slipped malicious instructions into the generative AI tools of more than 90 organizations, turning trusted assistants into engines for stealing credentials and even cryptocurrency, according to CrowdStrike’s 2026 Global Threat Report.
    • Industry observers note that that layer now has a name.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Joan Vendrell, NeuralTrust CEO and cofounder, has 15+ years of technology leadership experience advancing enterprise-grade AI security.

    ​In 2025, attackers slipped malicious instructions into the generative AI tools of more than 90 organizations, turning trusted assistants into engines for stealing credentials and even cryptocurrency, according to CrowdStrike’s 2026 Global Threat Report. What those incidents had in common wasn’t an exotic exploit but a missing layer of control between the application and the model.

    Industry observers note that that layer now has a name. As the number of models, co-pilots and agents multiplies, teams stop wiring every application directly to every provider and put an AI gateway in between. Gartner analysts describe it as an “intermediary between applications and AI services” that becomes a central point for “security, governance and observability.” The direction is right, but the way most organizations build that layer first is where the trouble starts.​.

    Sources indicate that in most early rollouts, the gateway is treated as a routing and cost-control layer that load-balances across providers and tracks spend. Security is assumed to be happening elsewhere, inside the application, at the model provider or in a review nobody actually scheduled, and that assumption is exactly where the exposure begins.

    In a recent development, the gateway has become the busiest and most privileged component in the AI stack, and adoption is no longer niche. Gartner researchers predict that 40% of enterprise applications will integrate task-specific AI agents by the end of 2026, up from less than 5% in 2025, and almost all of that traffic funnels through the gateway.

    Every prompt a user or agent sends, and every response a model returns, passes through it. It holds the API keys, the routing logic and, increasingly, the connections to email, file storage and CRM systems through the model context protocol (MCP). A component that sees all the traffic and holds all the credentials becomes either the strongest control point in the architecture or its single largest weakness.

    A gateway that moves requests faster without inspecting them industrializes the risk. The threats that matter most in AI are semantic, not merely network-level. In a prompt injection attack, an adversary hides an instruction inside content the model will later read, like a webpage, a PDF or an email, and the model can’t tell that planted instruction apart from a legitimate one and follows it.

    Neither a firewall, rate limiter nor gateway tuned only for latency and cost will catch that. CrowdStrike found that AI-enabled adversary operations rose 89% year over year, and that 82% of detections in 2025 involved no malware at all, a sign that attackers increasingly rely on manipulating language and trusted access rather than deploying traditional code. When an agent behind the gateway can call tools, read documents and reach production systems, a single injected instruction can convert legitimate access into data exfiltration or an unauthorized transaction. If the gateway forwards that traffic without inspecting prompts, tool calls and responses, the most central component in the stack is also the least aware.

    Sources indicate that the instinct is to add security later, as a separate product downstream, but that misses the point of interception, and the cost of that gap is measurable. IBM’s Cost of a Data Breach Report 2025 found that a high level of shadow AI added roughly $670,000 to the average breach, that 63% of breached organizations had no AI governance policy in place or were still developing one, and that 97% of organizations hit by an AI-related incident lacked appropriate AI access controls. These describe basic controls that were never wired into the path AI traffic travels.​​.

    Security that lives beside the gateway rather than inside it also splinters accountability. Access decisions happen in one system, content inspection in another and logging in a third, and none of them holds the full context of who called what through which model, which is precisely the seam attackers work.

    Recent findings suggest that the deployments that hold up under scrutiny share a few traits. The gateway inspects in-line and in both directions, screening prompts and tool calls for injection and policy violations before they reach a model, and screening responses for sensitive-data leakage before they return to a user or an agent. It enforces identity and least privilege for nonhuman callers, so agents and MCP connections are scoped as tightly as any employee because an overpermissioned agent is the modern version of a shared admin password. It treats consumption as a security signal and not only a billing one. And it produces a complete, queryable audit trail of every request, model, tool and data path in one place.

    That last trait is where the gateway earns its keep beyond security because regulators are converging on the same expectation. The EU AI Act, the NIST AI Risk Management Framework and ISO 42001 all assume you can demonstrate control and produce evidence of how your AI systems behave. A gateway that inspects and logs every interaction is the natural place to generate that evidence continuously, instead of reconstructing it under audit pressure.

    In a recent development, enterprises will keep centralizing AI traffic through gateways because the economics and operational simplicity are too strong to resist. The real decision is narrower, and it comes down to whether that central point is where policy is enforced, threats are caught and behavior is recorded, or merely a fast pipe that makes ungoverned traffic flow more efficiently.​.

While it doesn't guarantee against all losses and can't deliver the growth potential of stocks, it can provide a haven for cash you may need soon or to calm portfolio volatility.

    The idea behind adding a short-term bond ETF to a portfolio that relies mainly on stocks is simple. Companies matter stocks to raise money, a deal that can work out well for all parties as long as the company performs well.

    However, stock prices can fall sharply if investors fear weaker profits or a slowing economy. In fact, it doesn't take much more than a weak rumor or a poorly researched news story to scare some investors off.

    Recent findings suggest that in contrast, since SGOV holds U.S. government debt, performance is driven more by short-term interest rates and Treasury income than by corporate earnings or how everyday investors feel about the stock market.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Mortgage rates dropped today, but anything above 7% still puts pressure on home buyers’ budgets.

    The average interest rate on a 30-year, fixed-rate mortgage dropped to 7.24% APR, according to rates provided to NerdWallet by Zillow. This is 14 basis points lower than yesterday and three basis points lower than a week ago. (A basis point is one one-hundredth of a percentage point.).

    A significant drop is eye-catching, but you should consider mortgage interest rates' overall direction, not just what's going on today. While the economy never sleeps, markets are closed on the weekends. The rates you see Friday are unlikely to change much (if at all) until Monday.

    Here are the average APRs we're seeing today, as well as movement over the past month for context:.

    » Take the next step: Compare mortgage rates from NerdWallet’s top lenders.

    Mortgage rates are constantly changing, since a major part of how rates are set depends on reactions to upcoming inflation reports, job numbers, Fed meetings, global news ... you name it. For example, even tiny changes in the bond market can shift mortgage pricing.

    According to recent reports, next week, the Nerds are waiting for the Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index, due out Wednesday. It's the Federal Reserve's preferred measure of inflation, so investors will be watching closely. The Fed doesn't set mortgage rates, but lenders anticipate its decisions, so mortgage rates often move before the Fed acts. Stubbornly high inflation is a substantial reason why we’re seeing upward pressure on mortgage rates right now.

    If PCE shows inflation comes in hotter than expected, mortgage rates could climb as markets anticipate further Fed rate hikes. (An increase to the federal funds rate is already widely expected at the Fed’s Dec. 8-9 meeting.) A cooler reading could ease some pressure on mortgage rates for now.

    Sources indicate that I’m not getting my hopes up too high for meaningfully lower inflation, though. Last week's Producer Price Index showed wholesale inflation climbed 6.5% over the past year — its fastest pace in four years. Wholesale inflation measures the price businesses pay for things. When businesses’ costs go up, they could pass those along to consumers in the form of higher prices — keeping the flames of inflation alive.

    Whether Wednesday's PCE brings relief or another helping of bad inflation news, we'll know before the turkey hits the table on Thursday.

    Refinancing might make sense if today’s rates are at least 0.5 to 0.75 of a percentage point lower than your current rate (and if you plan to stay in your home long enough to break even on closing costs).

    With rates where they are right now, you may want to start considering a refi if your current rate is around 7.74% or higher.

    In a recent development, also consider your goals: Are you trying to lower your monthly payment, shorten your loan term or turn home equity into cash? For example, you might be more comfortable with paying a higher rate for a cash-out refinance than you would for a rate-and-term refinance, so long as the overall costs are lower than if you kept your original mortgage and added a HELOC or home equity loan.

    If you're looking for a lower rate, use NerdWallet's refinance calculator to estimate savings and understand how long it would take to break even on the costs of refinancing.

    In a recent development, » Time to refi? Compare refinance rates from NerdWallet’s top lenders.

    There is no universal “right” time to start shopping — what matters is whether you can comfortably afford a mortgage now at today’s rates.

    If the answer is yes, don’t get too hung up on whether you could be missing out on lower rates later; you can refinance down the road. Focus on getting preapproved, comparing lender offers, and understanding what monthly payment works for your budget.

    NerdWallet’s affordability calculator can help you estimate your potential monthly payment. If a upcoming home isn’t in the cards right now, there are still things you can do to strengthen your buyer profile. Take this time to pay down existing debts and build your down payment savings. Not only will this free up more cash flow for a future mortgage payment, it can also get you a better interest rate when you’re ready to buy.

    » Is now a good time to buy? See NerdWallet’s analysis.

    Industry observers note that if you already have a quote you’re happy with, you should consider locking your mortgage rate, especially if your lender offers a float-down option. A float-down lets you take advantage of a better rate if the market drops during your lock period.

    Rate locks protect you from increases while your loan is processed, and with the market forever bouncing around, that peace of mind can be worth it.

    🤓 Nerdy Reminder: Rates can change daily, and even hourly. If you’re happy with the deal you have, it’s okay to commit.

    Jensen Huang Returns. What Comes Next For Nvidia?

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1339 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Nvidia (NVDA +31.21%) shareholders have been through quite a lot over the past couple of weeks, and Monday morning brought a development few people would have predicted just days ago.
    • 23, Nvidia announced that its board had voted unanimously to reinstate Huang as CEO, reversing a decision that had sent shock waves through the manufacturer and the broader market.
    • For shareholders who watched Nvidia's stock tumble amid the uncertainty surrounding Huang's departure, today's news probably comes as an enormous relief.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By The Premium Team – Nov 23, 2026 at 11:05AM EST.

    Nvidia (NVDA +31.21%) shareholders have been through quite a lot over the past couple of weeks, and Monday morning brought a development few people would have predicted just days ago.

    Jensen Huang is back. Call it an early Thanksgiving gift.

    On Nov. 23, Nvidia announced that its board had voted unanimously to reinstate Huang as CEO, reversing a decision that had sent shock waves through the manufacturer and the broader market. The market responded enthusiastically, sending Nvidia shares up more than 30% and helping fuel a remarkable rebound across AI-related stocks.

    For shareholders who watched Nvidia's stock tumble amid the uncertainty surrounding Huang's departure, today's news probably comes as an enormous relief. It's easy to understand why. Investors have spent the past couple of weeks contemplating what Nvidia might look like without him. Now, at least for the moment, they don't have to.

    Remember that the stock market is constantly adjusting its expectations about what might happen next.

    Sources indicate that when Huang resigned on Nov. 12 amid revelations about his personal conduct and concerns involving a possible foreign intelligence effort, shareholders suddenly had to account for risks they hadn't anticipated. Nvidia faced an unexpected leadership transition at a particularly consequential moment in its history, along with regulatory uncertainty and questions about whether the controversy might damage the firm's long-term competitive position.

    Some of those concerns became less pressing this morning.

    With Huang returning, the market can reasonably feel more confident that Nvidia will keep executing the strategy he's known for, one that has proved effective in the market's eyes.

    In a recent development, that alone helps explain why so many people were eager to buy the stock. There may be some additional forces at work, too. Traders who had bet against Nvidia could be rushing to cover their positions, while momentum traders may be adding to the buying. Still, the enthusiasm surrounding his return speaks volumes about the value placed on his leadership.

    That brings us to what may be the most interesting part of today's announcement.

    Sources indicate that as recently as Nov. 17, Nvidia's board chair, Harvey Jones, said publicly that the board did not intend to reinstate Huang. Less than a week later, the directors unanimously voted to bring him back. That's an extraordinary change of direction, particularly given the circumstances surrounding his departure. We don't know everything that happened behind the scenes, but several developments may have influenced the board.

    According to recent reports, for one, the pressure to reinstate Huang was substantial. More than 180,000 people signed a petition supporting his return, including Elon Musk. President Donald Trump also publicly advocated for reinstatement, arguing that Huang's leadership was important to both Nvidia and the United States.

    Sources indicate that nvidia's announcement confirms that its board received input from senior levels of the U.S. government. Based on that input, the directors said they were confident that reinstating Huang posed no national security risk.

    But perhaps the most consequential consideration was the potential cost of losing Huang himself.

    Sources indicate that for all the controversy surrounding his departure, Nvidia's directors may have concluded that the business risks of replacing their founder were simply too great. Finding someone who could take over Huang's responsibilities would be difficult enough. Finding someone who could replicate his particular combination of technological vision, industry relationships, and institutional knowledge might be considerably harder.

    That's a reasonable shareholder-value argument. Nvidia has not publicly attributed its decision to any one of these factors. Even so, the reversal raises a question.

    If Nvidia depends so heavily on Huang that losing him threatens an enormous amount of shareholder value, how much independence does its board really have when it comes to holding him accountable?

    After all, the directors' responsibility is to oversee management on behalf of shareholders, and that responsibility doesn't disappear because the CEO happens to be exceptionally talented or influential.

    It has been revealed that it's entirely possible that Nvidia's board carefully weighed the available evidence and sincerely concluded that reinstatement was the best decision for the manufacturer. But given the speed of the reversal and the intense political and investor pressure surrounding it, it's fair to wonder whether the board can exercise sufficient independence from its founder.

    Nvidia's announcement includes another vital detail.

    The independent investigation into the circumstances surrounding Huang's departure is continuing.

    The board notes it is satisfied with Huang's candor and ability to lead the manufacturer following a series of discussions with him. Nvidia also says it will continue cooperating with ongoing government investigations.

    According to recent reports, meanwhile, the firm is taking additional steps to strengthen oversight. It has established a board committee focused on national security and export controls and is searching for a new chief compliance officer.

    These measures suggest the directors recognize that the firm faces important responsibilities beyond deciding who occupies the CEO's office.

    Sources indicate that it's worth emphasizing that Huang has not been charged with a crime. The existence of an investigation should never be treated as proof of wrongdoing.

    In a recent development, at the same time, investors should recognize that the board's endorsement today isn't a final legal exoneration. If the ongoing investigation produces evidence that changes the directors' understanding of what happened, they could find themselves confronting another difficult decision about Huang's future.

    In certain enforcement cases, the SEC can also seek orders barring individuals from serving as officers or directors of public companies, although there's no reason to assume that such an outcome is likely here.

    In a recent development, the broader point is that Nvidia has restored some stability to its leadership without resolving all the uncertainty surrounding the company. And depending on what the investigations ultimately uncover, some of those unresolved concerns could become more consequential.

    We can understand why the market is celebrating. Nvidia's leadership crisis introduced a tremendous amount of uncertainty into an already volatile market, and Huang's return addresses one of the most immediate concerns. But we would be reluctant to interpret the stock's rebound as evidence that everything is back to normal.

    Today's buying tells us that the market feels considerably better about Nvidia's prospects with Huang back in charge. It doesn't tell us whether reinstating him was the right governance decision, whether the outstanding investigations will vindicate him, or whether the manufacturer has done enough to address the risks exposed by this episode.

    For Foolish investors, it's also worth separating the excitement of the moment from the reasons they might have invested in Nvidia in the first place.

    The company still needs to sustain its technological lead, capitalize on the enormous demand for AI computing, maintain its relationships with customers, and deliver the earnings growth necessary to justify its valuation. Huang's return may improve confidence in Nvidia's ability to do those things, but it doesn't guarantee their success.

    There's also a lesson here about the risks of investing in a organization whose identity and success are so closely associated with one person. Huang's leadership has undoubtedly been an extraordinary asset for Nvidia. The events of the past two weeks have also demonstrated how vulnerable the company may be to uncertainty surrounding him.

    So while today's news offers plenty of reason to feel relieved, we wouldn't put the entire controversy behind us just yet.

    Sources indicate that huang is back at the helm of Nvidia, and the market seems delighted to have him there. Whether the company emerges from this episode with stronger governance and a more resilient business remains to be seen.

    That's something we'll be watching long after today's excitement fades.

    #142340. Why Retaining Top Tech Talent Is About The Mission, Not Just Money

    📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (935 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Forbes ↗ Open Full Page

    Why Retaining Top Tech Talent Is About The Mission, Not Just Money

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (935 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Forbes

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Jamie Smith is Chief Information Officer at the University of Phoenix.
    • ​For years, too many tech managers have operated under the misguided belief that the best engineers follow the money.
    • However, while compensation definitely matters, it’s not as much as many leaders assume.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Jamie Smith is Chief Information Officer at the University of Phoenix.

    ​For years, too many tech managers have operated under the misguided belief that the best engineers follow the money. If a competitor offers a bigger compensation package, the thinking goes, then it’s time to say goodbye to your top performers. This belief has shaped everything from recruiting strategies to retention budgets. ​.

    However, while compensation definitely matters, it’s not as much as many leaders assume.

    For the top-tier engineers and tech talent you are trying to retain, the key factors are often less about numbers and more about the human qualities: autonomy, growth and work-life balance.​ According to a recent ISACA survey, about the same number of technology professionals cited compensation (28%) as the reason they left their previous job as better career prospects (29%) and looking for more interesting work (23%).

    In an age of AI, listening to what people actually want from their jobs is one of the easiest—and most effective—ways to hold down the workplace turnover rate.​.

    According to recent reports, as the manager of a tech staff of 300, I know what it’s like to fend off a steady parade of poaching recruiters from the Magnificent Seven tech giants. I can’t match their budgets, but what I do know is that many of the strongest engineers aren’t motivated exclusively by financial reward.

    They want challenges, difficult problems to solve and a commitment from leadership to actually do it. They want the opportunity and responsibility to make a major difference, not to be just a face in the crowd that worked on incremental change.​.

    And perhaps most importantly, these high performers want the freedom to decide how to solve those problems.​.

    Industry observers note that managers often underestimate the power of autonomy. From what I’ve seen, talented employees rarely leave because they are working too independently. More often, they leave because layers of process, bureaucracy and approvals make it difficult to do their best work. The most effective leaders understand that their job is not to control every decision, but to create an environment where talented people can move promptly and confidently.

    That lesson is becoming more crucial as AI transforms software development. Engineers with generative AI tools are discovering they can prototype, test and deploy solutions at a pace that would have been unimaginable just a few years ago.

    Once employees experience that acceleration, they will become far less tolerant of friction. Every unnecessary meeting, approval process or organizational red tape feels magnified.​ When organizations make that difficult, those employees will start looking elsewhere.​​.

    One of the most powerful retention strategies is hiring people who connect with the organization’s purpose. According to 2022 Qualtrics research, employees who see their own experiences reflected in the company’s mission are less likely to desire to leave their role. They are not simply working for a paycheck. They are contributing to a goal that feels personally meaningful.​.

    It has been revealed that that does not mean every employee must view their job as a calling. But during the hiring process, leaders should spend more time evaluating mission alignment. Good companies can always teach technical skills. Dedication to a company’s purpose is much harder to manufacture after the fact.​.

    The war for talent often focuses on recruiting experienced professionals from competitors, yet many organizations overlook extraordinary talent already on their payrolls.

    We’ve found them in our own workplace: the customer service representative who taught herself to build automation tools to streamline her job, the internal IT technician who automated diagnostics with AI, the career changer who brings a unique perspective from another industry.​.

    To add talent, some of the most successful companies have shifted from a buy strategy to a make strategy: investing in internal development, apprenticeships, mentorship programs and career mobility.

    I believe this strategy is not only cost-effective but also creates stronger loyalty. Employees are more likely to stay when they feel their employer is actively investing in their growth.​.

    This may be the hardest lesson for managers to accept: Sometimes, talented employees leave for reasons that have nothing to do with dissatisfaction. They want to join a startup. They want to work at a global technology giant. They want a newly introduced challenge.

    Trying to prevent every departure can become a distraction from building your own healthy and evolving culture.​ Smart leaders understand that retention is not about creating handcuffs, but about creating a workplace people want to return to.​.

    Former employees often become future employees. The engineer who leaves for a startup may eventually come back with valuable new skills and experiences. The developer who joins a major technology company may later realize that larger organizations offer less responsibility, less visibility and less impact than they expected.​.

    That reality highlights one final truth about retaining high performers: Responsibility itself is a benefit.​.

    Many engineers would rather own a meaningful product than manage a tiny piece of a gigantic machine. They want to see the consequences of their work, to have direct influence over outcomes and to know that their contributions matter.​.

    According to recent reports, the battle for talent is not always decided by offering the biggest paycheck. Instead, to retain top employees, employers should combine competitive compensation with meaningful responsibility, authentic mission, professional growth, work-life balance and the autonomy to do great work.​.

    In other words, the future of retention is not about paying people more. It is about giving them more reasons to stay.​​.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Robinhood shares were down around 8% in pre-market trading on Wednesday as investors digested weaker-than-expected third-quarter earnings despite growth in options trading and prediction markets.

    Recent findings suggest that here's how the brokerage performed in its quarter ended Sept. 30, compared with Wall Street estimates, based on a survey of analysts by LSEG:.

    According to recent reports, robinhood's net income fell to $468 million, or 51 cents per share, from $556 million, or 61 cents per share, a year ago. Revenue represented a 12% increase from $1.27 billion in the same quarter last year.

    Despite that gain, transaction-based revenue of $867 million came in below Wall Street estimates from StreetAccount of $879 million, putting focus on whether Robinhood can sustain momentum across its trading businesses and reduce its reliance on volatile market activity.

    Sources indicate that robinhood has been diversifying its business as it tries to expand its brokerage app into a broader financial services platform. Options trading and event contracts have become increasingly important sources of transaction revenue, while the firm has continued to invest in wealth management, subscriptions and other offerings.

    Transaction-based revenue grew 19% from the same period last year to $867 million, driven primarily by a more than 500% increase in event contracts revenue. Additionally, options revenue grew 31% to $399 million and equities revenue rose 41% to $121 million.

    Those gains were partially offset by cryptocurrency revenue, which fell 55% to $120 million.

    Chief Financial Officer Shiv Verma told CNBC event contracts on crypto movements did well in the quarter, offering investors another way to express a view on crypto despite the slump in prices and spot trading.

    Net deposits on the Robinhood platform totaled $15.7 billion for the quarter, equal to a 17% annualized growth rate based on total platform assets at the end of Q2 2026. Over the past year, net deposits totaled $71 billion, representing 21% growth compared with total platform assets at the end of Q3 2025.

    —With reporting from CNBC's Robert Hum and Kate Rooney.

    • The approach you take to building a retirement portfolio should hinge on where you are in your savings journey.
    • Recent findings suggest that if you're now within a few years of retirement, your portfolio may require a closer look.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Maurie Backman – Nov 23, 2026 at 11:09AM EST.

    The approach you take to building a retirement portfolio should hinge on where you are in your savings journey. When you're in your 30s, 40s, or 50s, and retirement is more than a decade away, it often makes sense to go heavy on stocks to grow your money efficiently. But as retirement nears, your strategy should shift.

    Recent findings suggest that if you're now within a few years of retirement, your portfolio may require a closer look. Here are two key moves to make.

    Investing in stocks can be a great way to supercharge your IRA or 401(k). But stocks can be extremely volatile.

    Recent findings suggest that when you're not tapping your retirement savings for income, that's not a problem. Sure, it's not fun to watch your portfolio value swing wildly, but it's part of the process. But once you're at the point where your portfolio becomes an income stream, it's important to limit volatility so you're able to access funds when you need to.

    According to recent reports, to that end, think about a reduced stock allocation you're comfortable with. You may decide to keep 60% of your portfolio in stocks and put the rest in bonds and cash. Or, you may feel comfortable with a larger stock allocation.

    Recent findings suggest that one thing you don't want to do, though, is unload stocks entirely. You want your portfolio to continue growing in retirement so it can keep up with inflation.

    If you're living off your savings in retirement and the market crashes, selling assets could mean locking in permanent portfolio losses. That's not what you want. To avoid that scenario, build a cash buffer so you can cover your expenses for a period without having to sell any assets whose value has dropped.

    It has been revealed that the amount of cash you keep on hand should depend on your income needs, how flexible your budget is, and how much non-portfolio income you have, such as Social Security. A good rule of thumb, though, is to keep one to three years' worth of living costs in cash in case of a prolonged market slump.

    If you get large Social Security checks that cover most of your costs, you may be fine to stick to the lower end of that range. If your benefits only cover a small portion of your bills, the larger end may be more appropriate.

    Industry observers note that you no doubt worked hard to build your portfolio. Now, you need to make sure it's set up to serve you well in retirement. So if you're nearing that stage, these are two moves you don't want to gloss over.

    #142335. Industry News: College Scholarship Breakdown: Types, Sponsors and Eligibility at a Glance

    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1396 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Nerdwallet ↗ Open Full Page

    Industry News: College Scholarship Breakdown: Types, Sponsors and Eligibility at a Glance

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1396 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nerdwallet

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, scholarships have become a standard part of applying for college.
    • Before you go searching for a scholarship, it's notable to understand the types of scholarships available and how to identify the ones that give you the best chance of winning, which can save you time and potentially earn you more funding.
    • Recent findings suggest that scholarships are often funded by three groups: private organizations, institutions like universities, and government agencies.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, scholarships have become a standard part of applying for college. You can learn about scholarships in a variety of ways, but looking through an online database of available scholarships — the most common way — can be overwhelming.

    Before you go searching for a scholarship, it's notable to understand the types of scholarships available and how to identify the ones that give you the best chance of winning, which can save you time and potentially earn you more funding. Here’s what you need to know about scholarships to decide which ones are best for you.

    Recent findings suggest that scholarships are often funded by three groups: private organizations, institutions like universities, and government agencies. None is better than the other when it comes to awarding funds.

    Nonprofit organizations and clubs that are looking for students either majoring in or researching certain fields, or who have experience volunteering in a specific field.

    Companies that want to support all students or only fund those majoring in a field that relates to the companies’ industries.

    Financial institutions, such as banks or credit unions, that want to support their community or their members.

    Individuals or families that are funding private scholarships, usually in memory of a loved one.

    Universities and colleges that are offering funds to students who attend their campuses.

    Research organizations that want to fund students who will research in their areas of interest and further their causes.

    Sources indicate that these scholarships generally are provided by local, state or federal government agencies for a variety of reasons. Despite being funded by a government agency, the scholarships do not require you to pay back the money — unlike federal student loans.

    Some scholarships pay for anything related to college expenses, including tuition, room and board, books and supplies, and more. Other scholarships limit what you can pay for with the funds, such as only tuition or tuition along with books. It’s important to look at this restriction when applying for scholarships to ensure the funds will go toward what you need to cover.

    Recent findings suggest that merit scholarships require you to show excellence or achievements in your schoolwork, through talents and abilities, and even leadership or service work. Because these types of awards can be highly competitive, merit scholarships might require more than just achievements, such as volunteer or leadership experience. This means merit-based scholarships can overlap with other types of scholarship categories. Here are some examples of merit-based scholarships:.

    Merit scholarships often require you to have earned a minimum grade point average (GPA). The minimum GPA depends on the scholarship but often ranges from 2.0 to 4.0, with more competitive scholarships usually requiring higher GPAs. Scholarships with lower GPA minimums are more likely to consider additional factors, such as financial need.

    Some merit scholarships might require a minimum ACT or SAT score instead of a GPA — or in addition to a minimum GPA.

    Merit scholarships might also require applicants to have participated in activities outside of their schoolwork. This is common for scholarships that require membership in a certain group or organization. For example, membership in agricultural clubs, such as 4-H or FFA, and scouting groups, such as the National Eagle Scout Association, appear in scholarship requirements.

    According to recent reports, some scholarships emphasize volunteering or community service and only consider applicants who have that experience. Applications vary in how detailed their requirements can be. Some scholarships want only a general description of where and how you’ve volunteered, and others might require experience with a service project that shows more leadership experience or time volunteering with a certain type of organization.

    Scholarships that are awarded to students who can’t afford college are called need-based scholarships.

    Industry observers note that unmet financial need is the difference between what it will cost you to attend college and what you can afford to pay. Because calculating how much you can afford is a complicated process, many scholarships refer to your FAFSA to document your financial need.

    It has been revealed that some scholarship requirements may be as straightforward as demonstrating that you have financial need, but some scholarships might have income limits. However, income restrictions are less common.

    It has been revealed that athletic scholarships are for — you guessed it — athletes. They are usually offered by colleges and universities to recruit athletes onto their collegiate teams and can be competitive. Which sports have scholarships available and the scholarship amounts vary by college.

    Sources indicate that even though the main criterion for an athletic scholarship is being good at your sport, you’ll likely still need to show that you can keep up with your schoolwork. Most athletic scholarships require students to earn a minimum GPA or test scores to remain eligible while they’re in college.

    Some scholarships are designated for students majoring in a general field, such as science or education, but others can be for very specific areas of study. For example, a scholarship for students majoring in a natural resource field could include majors in biology, ecology, wildlife biology, conservation education, forestry, soils and hydrology. However, a stricter scholarship might state that students have to major in more specific topics, such as biochemistry or microbial ecology.

    According to recent reports, scholarships are available for active and former members of the military and members of their families. In addition to federal funds available for veterans to attend college, private organizations and some universities have scholarships for veterans to offset the cost of a degree.

    Sources indicate that which family members can apply for funds depends on the individual scholarship. For example, some scholarships extend to children or spouses of veterans, but some go as far in a family tree as great-grandchildren.

    It has been revealed that veteran- and military-focused scholarships might require that applicants or their family members enlisted in a certain branch, served during a particular time or conflict, or meet a certain rank or status such as receiving disability. Scholarships might also require that the applicant be a wartime veteran or family member of a wartime veteran; not all veterans meet this status.

    In a recent development, scholarships are also awarded to people who identify with a certain group. Common examples of identity-based scholarships include those for people who have disabilities, belong to certain ethnic or religious groups, identify as LGBTQIA+ or are first-generation students. Some identity-based scholarships require applicants to meet several criteria, such as belonging to more than one identity group.

    Outside of what would be considered standard DEI groups, there are scholarships for applicants who identify with less common groups, such as veganism, homelessness and model railroad builders.

    Sources indicate that the best scholarships for you depend on your situation. For example, if you are a skilled athlete with a good academic record, going for an athletic scholarship might give you the most funding. On the other hand, if you’re going to research a topic that isn’t common, looking for scholarships that support your research topic might be your best bet because competition could be lower.

    Good tactics to figure out which scholarships are worth your time include:.

    In a recent development, think of the skills, talents, experience and identities that are unique to you. For example, being a child of a veteran immediately qualifies you for scholarships with fewer applicants than scholarships open to everyone. Likewise, if you embrace a certain ethnicity, identify with a specific group or have experience with a type of work, you might qualify for scholarships that appreciate and recognize those attributes more than the average scholarship.

    Recent findings suggest that apply if you think you're eligible. Don’t apply to just a few scholarships and hope you get them. Instead, apply for as many scholarships as you can and for which you’re eligible. This increases your chances of receiving funds. Even small scholarships can make a massive impact when you add several of them together.

    Understand how you can use the money. If you already have a scholarship that covers only books, applying for the same type of scholarship isn’t helpful if you don’t need the extra funds. Instead, look for scholarships that cover the costs you have remaining.

    Not sure where to look? Our sister site Scholarships360.org provides students with vetted scholarship opportunities. That would be a good place to start.

    Addas a preferred source on Google.

    #142332. Unleash Your People Instead Of Replacing Them: The Human Side Of The Agentic AI Revolution

    📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1000 w)
    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Forbes ↗ Open Full Page

    Unleash Your People Instead Of Replacing Them: The Human Side Of The Agentic AI Revolution

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1000 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Forbes

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Scott Alldridge is CEO of IP Services, a visionary leader, and author of the bestselling VisibleOps book and series.
    • In a recent development, much of the work AI is being used to automate today involves tasks that employees already perform.
    • This presents opportunities not only for financial growth but also for getting more out of the people who make the business successful.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Scott Alldridge is CEO of IP Services, a visionary leader, and author of the bestselling VisibleOps book and series.

    In a recent development, much of the work AI is being used to automate today involves tasks that employees already perform. Agentic AI creates an opportunity to automate work across applications and entire workflows, saving time for an organization’s most valuable assets: its employees.

    This presents opportunities not only for financial growth but also for getting more out of the people who make the business successful.

    Sources indicate that as a consultant in operations improvement for more than 15 years, I’ve seen firsthand that people are worth far more than their payroll figures. The amount of relationship building, creative work and critical thinking employees can contribute is far greater than the time they currently spend on routine tasks such as entering data and managing processes.

    Instead of asking how many employees AI can replace, CEOs should ask the reverse question: How much more could their employees accomplish if repetitive work were removed from their responsibilities?​.

    Recent findings suggest that ​Think about a typical small business. ​Marketing employees might spend most of their time preparing reports on leads. Customer service representatives document every call and answer repeated questions. Accounting employees process invoices and reconcile bank and credit card accounts.

    ​All of this work is necessary, but how much of it actually requires the creativity, relationship building and strategic decision making that employees could otherwise bring to the business?

    Industry observers note that ​Increasingly, much of this routine work can be automated. ​Consider what marketing employees could accomplish with that reclaimed time: strengthening relationships with clients, studying the competition in greater detail and creating more campaigns to generate revenue.

    ​The same opportunity exists across every department. When employees spend less time entering data and managing repetitive processes, they have more capacity to solve problems, serve customers and develop fresh opportunities for the firm. ​That, to me, is the real opportunity.

    ​Of course, CEOs lead for-profit companies, so labor costs, competitive pricing and thin profit margins will inevitably enter the equation.

    Sources indicate that ​An IDC study commissioned by Microsoft in 2024 estimated an average return of $3.70 for every $1 invested among organizations using generative AI in the study. This figure represents the average of the estimates provided by participating organizations. It’s also vital to recognize that generative AI refers to a broad category of AI, not specifically agentic AI.

    Recent findings suggest that ​For an organization developing and supporting fresh AI-enabled processes during the first year or so, including training employees to use them effectively, the goal might be to generate $37,000 in business value. ​That value could come from less overtime, fewer errors, lower contractor costs and sustained growth without an immediate need for additional headcount.

    According to recent reports, ​Simply giving an employee five hours back in their workweek doesn’t put extra cash in the bank. Their salary hasn’t changed. ​What has changed is their capacity. ​Can those additional hours translate into better customer service, fresh business opportunities or stronger relationships with existing customers?

    ​Published averages don’t automatically translate into savings or value for your employees. CEOs need to consider how reclaimed time will actually be used and how that contributes to the business.

    Sources indicate that ​Imagine discovering that AI could be configured to complete the majority of your daily work.​ Would you feel excited? Concerned? Afraid for your future?​.

    Recent findings suggest that ​Your employees have families, financial commitments and careers to worry about. If you introduce AI in a way that suggests its primary purpose is to reduce their workload, you risk creating suspicion about the technology before implementation has even begun.

    In a recent development, ​There is a better way. Ask employees to list the tasks in their daily routines that they perceive to be time-consuming or unnecessary. Then ask them to identify the projects and customer service improvements they have always wanted to pursue but never had the time to implement.

    ​It’s far more enjoyable and valuable for an employee to be able to say, “I have half of my previous routine work automated, and I can spend so much more time focusing on our customers,” than to spend that time worrying about being replaced by a machine.

    However, not every responsibility should be handed over to AI. For example, while AI can manage customer information, recommend actions and even send messages, handling an unhappy customer or training a latest employee still requires human judgment. Even the most complex AI systems need to be monitored, and a human must ultimately remain accountable for their decisions and actions.

    ​Sophisticated AI systems can still make mistakes in their processing. All access, decisions and actions by agentic AI require appropriate human oversight. A straightforward rule for AI governance is to automate tasks and to never automate accountability.​.

    The goal should be to free people to focus on the things that matter most to them and to the organization, whether that’s serving customers, improving services or developing fresh opportunities.

    Recent findings suggest that ​Some organizations will use agentic AI to reduce employee headcount. Others will use these technologies to serve more customers, strengthen their employees’ capabilities and create new opportunities for people to apply their skills.

    Recent findings suggest that ​Staffing reductions may happen, but they shouldn’t be the starting point for AI adoption. ​Before cutting headcount, eliminate the unnecessary work your employees are presently doing. Before replacing an employee with AI, consider the value that person could bring to the organization in a different role.

    ​Finally, don’t declare AI a success until you’ve measured its impact on profitability, productivity, customer value and employee value. When something as innovative as agentic AI can help people accomplish things they previously didn’t have the time or capacity to do, that’s more than just a technology strategy. It’s a leadership strategy.​​.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • By Brendan Coffey – Updated Nov 23, 2026 at 11:11AM EST.
    • 10 stocks we like better than Bristol Myers Squibb ›.
    • It has been revealed that choosing between two healthcare leaders requires a close look at their evolving drug portfolios and financial foundations.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Brendan Coffey – Updated Nov 23, 2026 at 11:11AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Bristol Myers Squibb ›.

    It has been revealed that choosing between two healthcare leaders requires a close look at their evolving drug portfolios and financial foundations. You must decide whether Bristol Myers Squibb (BMY +1.45%) or Johnson & Johnson (JNJ -0.11%) offers the better path for long-term growth.

    Sources indicate that both companies operate within the pharmaceutical stocks category, yet they serve different niches. Bristol Myers Squibb focuses heavily on biopharmaceuticals for serious diseases, while Johnson & Johnson offers a mix of medicines and surgical devices. These businesses are often compared due to their massive scale and importance to global healthcare infrastructure.

    It has been revealed that bristol Myers Squibb focuses on discovering and developing medicines for oncology, hematology, neuroscience, and cardiovascular diseases. The organization distributes its products to wholesalers, specialty pharmacies, and government agencies. It recently expanded its reach with direct-to-patient offerings for several drugs, providing roughly 80% discounts to cash-paying patients. Additionally, a December 2025 agreement with the U.S. government involves providing Eliquis to the Medicaid program for free and donating ingredients to the national reserve.

    Recent findings suggest that in the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached about $50 billion, representing growth of approximately 4.2% over the prior period. Net income for the same time frame was around $9.2 billion. This performance shows a recovery in profitability compared to certain prior periods. The manufacturer relies on its core segments to offset pricing pressures and changes in government healthcare policies.

    As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio was nearly 2.6x. This ratio, which measures total debt relative to shareholders' equity, suggests the organization uses a significant amount of borrowed capital. The current ratio of 1.3x compares short-term assets to short-term liabilities, indicating the company has enough resources to cover its upcoming obligations. In the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, free cash flow reached roughly $12.8 billion. Free cash flow is the cash left over after the business covers its day-to-day operations and equipment upgrades.

    Industry observers note that johnson & Johnson operates through two primary segments: Innovative Medicine and MedTech. Its Innovative Medicine division develops treatments for oncology, immunology, and neuroscience, while the MedTech arm provides surgical and orthopedic devices. The company serves a diverse group of customers, including hospitals, retailers, and healthcare professionals globally. It maintains an extensive global supply chain and frequently enters licensing agreements with strategic partners to co-develop upcoming products.

    In the 12 months ended Sept. 27, 2026, revenue reached approximately $99.3 billion. This was supported by revenue growth of nearly 7.8% compared to the previous year. Net income for the period was about $16.1 billion. These figures highlight the scale of the company, which continues to generate substantial profits across its various medical and technology segments.

    As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio was roughly 0.6x. This indicates a more conservative use of debt relative to its equity than many of its peers. The current ratio is approximately 1.0x, indicating that its short-term assets are roughly equal to its short-term liabilities. In the fiscal year ended Dec. 28, 2025, free cash flow was about $19.7 billion. This strong cash generation provides the company with flexibility for acquisitions and research and development initiatives.

    Bristol Myers Squibb faces intense pricing pressure from government policies such as the Inflation Reduction Act, which has led to price caps on key drugs like Eliquis and Orencia. Patent cliff risks are also significant, as generic versions of Revlimid and Eliquis threaten to take market share. The organization deals with high research and development failure rates and operational reliance on partners like BioNTech (BNTX +5.26%), Zai Lab (ZLAB +6.32%), Zenas BioPharma (ZBIO +5.58%), and Merck (MRK +0.86%). High debt levels from recent acquisitions like Karuna and RayzeBio also limit its financial flexibility.

    According to recent reports, johnson & Johnson faces extensive litigation over its talc-based products, which recently resulted in a $5.5 billion settlement. The company also deals with high competitive pressure and the impending loss of patent exclusivity for key products like Darzalex and Stelara. Regulatory scrutiny and evolving laws regarding artificial intelligence and cybersecurity pose ongoing compliance costs. Additionally, the strategy to separate its orthopedics business could present integration challenges and unforeseen financial costs in the coming years.

    Based on both Forward P/E and P/S ratio metrics, Bristol Myers Squibb appears more conservatively priced than Johnson & Johnson.

    Valuation metrics include those sourced from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) and may differ from those of other data providers.

    Johnson & Johnson is an overlooked behemoth compared with faster-growing biotech companies. The business has 28 products and platforms that generate more than $1 billion in annual revenue. Its pharmaceuticals arm, Innovative Medicine, has received two FDA approvals this year and has two more approved drug product launches in the E.U. and the U.S. The Innovative Medicine division accounts for 65% of JNJ's annual revenue and appears to have a robust pipeline beyond the pending products. MedTech, its other arm, sells a wide range of healthcare products, including wound care, surgical instruments and implants, hip and knee replacements, and spinal implants. The recent buy of Atraverse Medical bolsters that business. Revenue for Johnson & Johnson is expected to rise to $101 billion in the current fiscal year. However, Wall Street anticipates a $10 billion drop in net income, to around $16.6 billion.

    Bristol Myers Squibb, meanwhile, has made positive strides, with its newer growth brands gaining traction and some interesting candidates in the pipeline. The stock is cheap, and that seems to be for good reason. Investors have already priced in much of the upcoming difficulty, which softens the downside.

    Revenue for the current fiscal year should edge up 3% to $49.8 billion, with a much healthier rise in net income of more than 40% to $11.2 billion.

    Bristol Myers has attractively low forward price-to-earnings and price-to-sales ratios, but, of course, that reflects some continued rough sailing ahead. Johnson & Johnson does come at a bit of a premium to the average S&P 500 stock, but not so much as to be prohibitive. Still, the healthy rise in net income for Bristol Myers is a sign its rebound is underway. For 2027, go with BMY.

    • In a recent development, it has been a wild few weeks on Wall Street for massive tech.
