    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Keithen Drury – Nov 23, 2026 at 11:12AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Apple ›.

    In a recent development, it has been a wild few weeks on Wall Street for massive tech. Many of the leading stocks in the sector are down significantly from their all-time highs -- but not Apple (AAPL +1.57%). The iPhone maker has been resilient amid the sell-off, and it's not hard to understand why: Its lack of artificial intelligence exposure.

    Industry observers note that this isn't necessarily a bad thing, and Apple isn't ignoring AI; it's just approaching the trend in a different way from its megacap peers. While most of Apple's peers are sinking hundreds of billions of dollars annually into building AI data centers, Apple has chosen to stay on the sidelines and instead deploy an AI model from one of these companies. This may cost it an incremental amount of money over the long term for each Apple device on which AI is deployed, but it spares it from having to spend a lot now.

    It has been revealed that this discipline has earned Apple a ton of respect on the market, and it's why the stock remains near its all-time high. But is it still a buy?

    In a recent development, apple has long been known as an excellent steward of its resources, and its actions over the past few years have been a display of that. It appears to have made a smart decision regarding AI, and the market has rewarded its stock for that.

    NASDAQ · As of 11:49 AM ET 11/23/26.

    According to recent reports, but the problem is the market may have gone too far in its appreciation. Apple is now one of the more expensive tech stocks on the market. When we use next year's expected earnings to value the stock, it has a huge premium over its peers.

    AAPL PE Ratio (Forward) data by YCharts.

    With companies like Nvidia (NVDA +31.21%) trading at 10 times next year's earnings or Alphabet (GOOG +5.76%) (GOOGL +6.22%) at 18 times, there is a clear premium being placed on Apple's stock.

    NVDA PE Ratio (Forward 1y) data by YCharts.

    NVDA PE Ratio (Forward 1y) data by YCharts.

    According to recent reports, the question investors must ask themselves is whether Apple is worth paying a forward P/E that's more than three times Nvidia's or double the valuation of Taiwan Semiconductor (TSM +15.01%). Even Amazon (AMZN +3.63%) is discounted compared to Apple.

    Recent findings suggest that of those, I'd pick Nvidia for the most upside, but there are also some other stories driving its price. Instead, I think Taiwan Semiconductor is the best pick of this bunch, as it will thrive regardless of which firm is designing the chips it manufactures or which clients are buying them.

    For me, 33 times next year's earnings is just too high of a premium to pay for Apple, especially when its peers trade for fractions of that. While I understand investors' hesitation about investing in Nvidia amid the tumultuous period it just experienced (and perhaps even now, with CEO Jensen Huang reinstated), companies like Taiwan Semiconductor and Alphabet are still full steam ahead with strong growth prospects. With market sentiment currently bearish on AI, now is the time to scoop up these AI companies, as that bearish sentiment likely won't last forever, especially if they continue reporting excellent results quarter after quarter.

    It has been revealed that apple stock has remained strong by staying out of the AI arena. But I think its valuation is just too high right now to invest in it.

    Dreading Holiday Money Talks With Family? Here's What to Say

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (816 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nerdwallet

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Holiday gatherings have a way of stirring up difficult and downright uncomfortable conversations — and not just about politics or cousin Derek’s love life.
    • Sources indicate that relatives and friends may also bring up their money troubles and financial aims.
    • It’s easy to feel obligated or pressured to help out.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Holiday gatherings have a way of stirring up difficult and downright uncomfortable conversations — and not just about politics or cousin Derek’s love life.

    Sources indicate that relatives and friends may also bring up their money troubles and financial aims. That might involve asking you to lend money or your credit.

    It’s easy to feel obligated or pressured to help out. But it’s important to establish boundaries so you don’t end up making a decision you’ll regret.

    Industry observers note that if you suspect a money request is coming your way, think carefully about what you’re willing — and able — to offer. You might choose a specific dollar limit or to give no financial help at all.

    “Only lend what you're truly OK losing,” says Alvin Carlos, a certified financial planner at District Capital Management in Washington, D.C. “Look at your budget and decide what you could hand over and never see again.”.

    Recent findings suggest that choose the language that best fits your situation. Adapt your responses as needed to guide the conversation in a direction that works for you.

    Recent findings suggest that “I understand that you need help. I just need to review my own finances before I can give you an answer. I’ll get back to you by [day].”.

    If the request comes up at a holiday or family gathering:.

    “I’d rather discuss this privately. Let’s find another time to talk.”.

    “Here's what I’m comfortable with, and here's what I have to protect to be financially safe, mentally safe, and to continue to be there for you in the ways that you need me.”Or, if you want to be more direct:.

    Sometimes, there’s an unspoken expectation to give money because of how much loved ones think you earn, states Ashley Agnew, a certified financial therapist in Boston.

    Getting ahead of it before there's a tipping point can help with tricky dynamics, she claims.

    Sources indicate that A recent Edward Jones report found that only about one-third of financial caregiving arrangements were planned and discussed in advance. The report also found that nearly half of financial caregivers (49%) make financial sacrifices, such as reducing or stopping saving, or tapping into their retirement account.

    Factor your financial health, your values and emotional well-being into your decision:.

    In a recent development, review your income, expenses and savings. If you provide financial help and don’t get the money back, would you struggle to pay bills or reach financial goals? Prioritize building an emergency fund, saving for retirement and paying off high-interest debt first, Carlos states.

    Consider your relationship. Would you feel resentful if you aren’t repaid? How do you think your friend or relative would react if you decline to help? Could it damage your relationship, and if so, is it worth it?

    Understand the credit risks. Co-signing or allowing someone else to use your credit can leave you responsible for payments and expose you to potential credit damage.

    Industry observers note that know the tax implications. If you’re considering a substantial gift or loan, check with a tax professional about any reporting requirements and tax consequences.

    Consult your partner. If you share finances, make sure to include your partner in your decision-making process, Agnew notes. If you have a parent asking for financial assistance, for example, but your cultural view is different from your spouse's, that’s a big opportunity for a rift.

    Industry observers note that aim to be clear and direct. When in doubt, keep your answer concise, Agnew claims.

    “Keeping it short and sweet will communicate that you've made a decision, not that you've requested a negotiation.”.

    Depending on where you left the conversation, you might have more steps to take.

    Recent findings suggest that stick to your boundaries and promises. Did you offer to contribute money? Pay as agreed. Did you say no? Don’t let your friend's or family member’s persistence, or the opinions of other friends and relatives, change your mind.

    If you offered to provide nonfinancial support, Carlos recommends pointing your loved one to local government and nonprofit resources. That might include emergency rent assistance, cheap or free financial advice, food banks and career services.

    Document the details and set the plan in motion. If you agreed to loan money, send your relative a quick text recapping the terms, Carlos notes. He also suggests setting up a simple repayment system together, such as a recurring Zelle or Venmo transfer.

    “Fewer reminders from you mean less tension,” he indicates.

    Industry observers note that get outside help, if necessary. Despite your best efforts, it can be difficult to handle the situation on your own. If you’re feeling lingering stress or your family can’t reach a resolution, you might want to bring in some help, Agnew claims.

    She recommends working with a financial therapist or advisor, or using a financial wellness app.

    Addas a preferred source on Google.

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (920 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, anthropic (ANT -2.34%) jumped 17.1% on Nov.
    • Here's why Anthropic could have an even larger impact on the broader stock market than SpaceX and how the IPO is impacting investors even if they don't initiative to buy Anthropic directly.
    • Sources indicate that the Nasdaq-100 is the 100 largest non-financial companies listed on the Nasdaq exchange by market cap.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Daniel Foelber – Nov 23, 2026 at 11:15AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Anthropic ›.

    According to recent reports, anthropic (ANT -2.34%) jumped 17.1% on Nov. 19 -- surpassing Space Exploration Technologies (SPCX +6.58%) as the largest initial public offering (IPO) in history after raising roughly $81.3 billion. However, SpaceX remains far more valuable, with a market cap of $1.88 trillion compared to $1.27 trillion for Anthropic.

    Here's why Anthropic could have an even larger impact on the broader stock market than SpaceX and how the IPO is impacting investors even if they don't initiative to buy Anthropic directly.

    Dario Amodei. Image source: Getty Images.

    Sources indicate that the Nasdaq-100 is the 100 largest non-financial companies listed on the Nasdaq exchange by market cap. SpaceX joined the Nasdaq-100 less than one month after going public thanks to the index's fresh fast-tracked rules that allow mega-cap companies to be added to the Nasdaq-100 after their 15th trading day. However, the S&P 500 (^GSPC +4.44%) still requires companies to be public for at least a year before they can be added.

    Anthropic is likely to be added to the Nasdaq-100 in early December, which will impact index-linked products like the Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ +6.34%). Several passively managed, high-profile exchange-traded funds (ETFs), including nine Vanguard ETFs, began buying SpaceX within weeks of its IPO. And I would expect the same for Anthropic.

    However, Anthropic's impact on the major indexes could be even larger than SpaceX's if it's classified as a tech stock.

    The tech sector makes up a staggering 64.4% of the Nasdaq-100 -- as measured by the Invesco QQQ Trust -- and 37.4% of the S&P 500. Despite it being a tech-focused company, Vanguard classified SpaceX in the communications sector alongside Alphabet (GOOG +5.76%) (GOOGL +5.73%) and Meta Platforms (META +6.06%). Similarly, Amazon (AMZN +3.23%) and Tesla (TSLA +12.52%) are in the consumer discretionary sector despite being tech-focused companies.

    If Anthropic is classified as a technology stock, it will make the Nasdaq-100 (and eventually the S&P 500) even more concentrated in the tech sector. It would also have far-reaching effects on market-cap-weighted tech sector ETFs -- which are larger than other sector ETFs. For example, the Vanguard Communications Services ETF (VOX +3.46%), which has added to its SpaceX holdings every month since it went public, has $5.4 billion in net assets, whereas the Vanguard Information Technology ETF (VGT +8.80%) has a staggering $145.1 billion in net assets. And that's just one investment management company's ETFs.

    NASDAQ · As of 11:45 AM ET 11/23/26.

    Anthropic plays a far more vital role in the artificial intelligence (AI) value chain than SpaceX. SpaceX owns xAI and has looks to build constellations of orbital data centers. But for now, most of its revenue comes from its Starlink network of broadband and mobile satellites. Anthropic arguably makes the most important family of large language models -- Claude.

    Anthropic is driving massive demand for compute capacity. It is a big reason why hyperscalers are aggressively investing in AI data centers, with ripple effects for chip companies and data center pick-and-shovel plays such as specialty machinery companies, industrials, utilities, and energy. In addition to Anthropic’s own demand for compute, many third-party AI agents and AI tools rely on foundational models like Claude, thereby amplifying the full impact on data center demand.

    Industry observers note that anthropic is much more notable to the market than its individual weighting will be in the major indexes. It's a similar dynamic to what we've seen play out with Nvidia (NVDA +31.21%). Jensen Huang's sudden resignation sparked a massive sell-off in companies that depend on or do business with Nvidia. And beyond that, Huang has been a major proponent of AI innovation and dealmaking, impacting financial markets far beyond Nvidia's own deals.

    So just as Nvidia is arguably the most key firm in the AI infrastructure layer of the value chain, Anthropic is probably the most vital company in the foundational model layer.

    With the market in a steep sell-off, some investors may view the Anthropic IPO as yet another factor that could add to volatility. And while the Anthropic IPO is arguably an even bigger risk to the market than the SpaceX IPO, it also has the potential to be an incredible opportunity.

    In a recent development, if Anthropic can continue delivering excellent revenue growth, it could be a catalyst for the broader tech sector and indexes. Especially if that growth coincides with more demand for even better AI chips, which would benefit the broader semiconductor industry.

    Investors interested in gaining exposure to Anthropic without buying the stock directly may want to consider a low-cost tech sector ETF like the Vanguard Information Technology ETF or the Vanguard Growth ETF (VUG +6.77%), which invests in growth stocks from all stock market sectors. These ETFs will likely gradually accumulate a larger stake in Anthropic as more shares are unlocked and sold by insiders and early investors on the Nasdaq.

    On the other hand, investors looking to avoid Anthropic altogether may want to stick with high-conviction individual stocks or value and non-tech sector ETFs.

    Latest Update: Engineering Trust: A Safe Path To Agentic AI In Utility Contact Centers

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (979 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Forbes

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Abhay Gupta is cofounder and CEO of Bidgely, evolving energy analytics for utilities with the power of data and artificial intelligence.
    • Recent findings suggest that ​Ten years ago, a routine utility call was simple: a customer wanted to pay a bill or report a neighborhood outage.
    • In a recent development, as grid modernization, time-of-use (TOU) tariffs and electrification continue to grow, customer conversations are becoming significantly more complex.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Abhay Gupta is cofounder and CEO of Bidgely, evolving energy analytics for utilities with the power of data and artificial intelligence.

    Recent findings suggest that ​Ten years ago, a routine utility call was simple: a customer wanted to pay a bill or report a neighborhood outage. Today, that same caller wants to know if charging their EV at midnight will cut their monthly bill, how to apply for a heat-pump rebate or whether their current electrical panel can handle rooftop solar.

    In a recent development, as grid modernization, time-of-use (TOU) tariffs and electrification continue to grow, customer conversations are becoming significantly more complex. Across the industry, this complexity reflects three broader shifts in how utilities must operate: shifting customer engagement, shifting load with confidence and shifting CapEx decisions.

    To navigate these shifts and keep pace with evolving needs, utilities have made impressive strides in expanding their digital toolkits. Online portals, automated Interactive Voice Response (IVR) systems and conversational Generative AI (GenAI) chatbots have successfully helped millions of customers perform routine self-service tasks—like checking account balances, verifying payment due dates or reporting service outages.

    According to recent reports, however, as utilities look to continuously enrich the customer experience and support load growth at a deeper level, the real win is moving from providing customers with information to empowering them to take immediate, verified action. While Gartner research shows that self-service interactions cost less than $2.00 per contact compared to $13.50 for live agents, standard self-service fully resolves only 14% of customer inquiries. Capturing that lost resolution is where the true value lies.

    Recent findings suggest that while Generative AI excels at summarizing complex rate schedules and synthesizing documents, Agentic AI executes complete end-to-end business workflows. Instead of telling a customer how to submit a request or directing them to a self-service web page, an AI agent securely reasons through multi-step tasks, connects directly with core enterprise systems and resolves requests on the spot.

    For the customer, this eliminates the frustration of multi-channel runarounds, phone tag and waiting days for back-office processing. For the utility, it transforms bottleneck operations into automated workflows that reduce overhead, drive down cost-to-serve and elevate overall customer satisfaction (CSAT) scores.

    When adding execution power to conversational interfaces, every touchpoint improves:.

    Digital Web Chat: Beyond answering basic questions, an AI agent analyzes meter data to explain usage spikes, matches the customer to the best rate and enrolls them in demand response programs on the spot.

    Voice Channels: Conversational voice replaces rigid phone trees with natural dialogue, securely verifying callers and completing service transfers, move orders or structured payment plans in real time.

    CSR Co-Pilot Support: When calls escalate, the AI acts as an assistant by passing complete context, pulling account history and drafting wrap-up notes so representatives can focus on customer empathy and high-value decision-making.

    Sources indicate that unlocking this level of execution requires moving past fragmented point solutions that overload IT teams. Instead, utilities need a unified approach that connects existing systems like CRM, meters and cloud data with specialized energy intelligence. By using secure APIs and modern integration protocols, utilities can embed targeted AI agents directly into everyday operational workflows.

    In my experience leading enterprise AI deployments, moving from conversational assistance to autonomous execution requires a much higher standard for governance, privacy and compliance.

    The primary hurdle is the utility tech stack. Most operations run on custom billing tools and siloed data platforms that were never built to talk to modern AI in real time. A single request like a rate switch requires pulling records across multiple legacy systems without dropping context. At the same time, letting an AI make changes to customer accounts on its own creates serious operational exposure. Beyond that, real customer requests are full of edge cases and an automated system can easily misinterpret complex billing disputes or unusual service exceptions. In a regulated industry, a single AI error or unauthorized change to a customer bill is a direct compliance liability.

    In a recent development, deploying autonomous systems safely does not mean accepting higher risk. It means engineering guardrails that prevent errors from happening in the first place. Here are three practical steps for utility technology leaders.

    The biggest mistake enterprise teams make is letting a language model make real-time decisions on business logic. Use the AI strictly for understanding intent, handling dialogue and organizing the workflow. All actual executions, such as issuing bill credits, switching rate intends or updating records, must run through hard-coded rules pre-approved by your legal and compliance teams. The AI handles the conversation, while proven business rules dictate the outcome.

    According to recent reports, be cautious about jumping straight to full autonomy. Start by deploying AI agents as co-pilots alongside your customer service team. Track accuracy, set clear confidence thresholds and evaluate edge cases in live advisory settings before letting agents resolve requests independently.

    Regulators demand transparency, especially during rate cases and commission reviews. Autonomous AI must run in secure, private cloud environments that protect customer data. More importantly, every reasoning step, system lookup and API call the AI makes must generate a clear, human readable audit log. Transparency turns compliance from a blocker into your strongest asset.

    The energy landscape is shifting from passive consumption to active customer participation, and contact center operations must evolve to match that reality. Ultimately, the best customer interaction is the one that never requires escalation and complex requests are resolved on the spot before friction builds.

    Sources indicate that by building a single intelligence foundation and treating AI as an autonomous execution partner rather than a simple answer engine, utility leaders can do far more than streamline back office queues. They can establish their organizations as trusted energy advisors that turn daily operational touchpoints into long-term customer trust.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • By Jake Lerch – Updated Nov 23, 2026 at 11:30AM EST.
    • As the world continues its steady shift toward digital commerce, investors are often torn between the established giants of the transaction world and the newer digital wallet innovators that changed how consumers shop.
    • Sources indicate that choosing between Mastercard (MA +1.66%) and PayPal (PYPL +2.69%) requires examining two distinct business models.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Jake Lerch – Updated Nov 23, 2026 at 11:30AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Mastercard ›.

    As the world continues its steady shift toward digital commerce, investors are often torn between the established giants of the transaction world and the newer digital wallet innovators that changed how consumers shop.

    Sources indicate that choosing between Mastercard (MA +1.66%) and PayPal (PYPL +2.69%) requires examining two distinct business models. While one operates a massive toll-booth network for global banks, the other provides a comprehensive platform for millions of consumers and merchants. This comparison explores which stock offers better value for the next few years.

    Mastercard operates as a central infrastructure provider among financial stocks. It provides the technology that connects banks, merchants, and consumers through its global payments network. The company generates revenue by charging small fees on every transaction processed across its infrastructure. Recently, it expanded its reach through partnerships with financial institutions like BMO and by building its brand as a naming partner for the McLaren Formula 1 Team.

    According to recent reports, in the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue was nearly $36.3 billion, representing a growth rate of roughly 15.3% compared to the previous period. This increase in sales helped the firm generate net income of approximately $17.0 billion. The company maintains a high net margin of nearly 46.7%, illustrating its ability to retain a significant portion of its revenue as profit.

    It has been revealed that as of its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is approximately 2.5x, meaning total debt is 2.5 times shareholder equity. The current ratio, which measures the ability to cover short-term liabilities with liquid assets, is roughly 1.0x. In the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, free cash flow was close to $16.4 billion. Free cash flow is the cash remaining after the business covers its day-to-day operations and capital investments.

    PayPal operates a two-sided platform that connects 439 million active accounts with merchants in approximately 200 markets worldwide. It offers a variety of services including digital wallets, person-to-person payments via Venmo, and merchant checkout solutions. The tech giant continues to evolve by offering newly introduced features, such as mass-disbursement services for creators and digital stablecoin services, to remain relevant in a changing financial landscape.

    In the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue was approximately $34.3 billion, representing growth of nearly 4.4%. Net income for this period was roughly $4.7 billion. While its top-line growth is slower than its rival, the manufacturer still maintains a net margin of close to 13.8%, demonstrating consistent profitability across its diverse payment markets.

    In a recent development, as of its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is approximately 0.5x, meaning total debt is half the value of shareholder equity. The current ratio is roughly 1.3x, suggesting the manufacturer has a comfortable cushion to meet its short-term financial obligations. In the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, free cash flow was nearly $5.6 billion, providing the company with capital for reinvestment or potential share buybacks.

    Mastercard faces intense competition from global payment networks such as Visa (V +2.09%), as well as upcoming fintech providers and government-backed payment systems. It is also subject to extensive global regulatory oversight regarding interchange fees and data localization. Significant legal risks exist, including a recent £5 billion lawsuit in the UK and ongoing antitrust litigation that could affect its future fee structures.

    PayPal competes with traditional banks and payment networks like American Express (AXP +1.90%), as well as specialized digital payment providers. The company manages operational risks related to potential cyberattacks and its dependence on third-party cloud and banking partners. Additionally, it carries credit risk associated with its consumer and merchant financing products and must navigate evolving regulations regarding cryptocurrency and artificial intelligence.

    PayPal appears more affordable than Mastercard based on its lower Forward P/E and its lower P/S ratio, which measures price against sales over the past twelve months.

    Valuation metrics include those sourced from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) and may differ from those of other data providers.

    When comparing Mastercard and PayPal, investors should consider a few key factors. Let's have a look at them and see what that tells us about each stock.

    Industry observers note that firstly, we should consider revenue growth. Over the last three years, PayPal has delivered average year-over-year revenue growth of 6.1%, while Mastercard has generated 14.2% revenue growth. Not only has Mastercard delivered a better average, but the gap has also widened in recent quarters. Mastercard continues to generate revenue growth around 14%, but PayPal's has slipped to about 1%. That gives Mastercard a significant lead in this category.

    Another factor to consider is each company's profitability. PayPal's operating margin is about 18.9%, indicating decent profitability. However, Mastercard's operating margin is an impressive 59.2%. That's yet another edge for the payment giant.

    Lastly, there's valuation. Since both companies are consistently profitable, we can examine their respective price-to-earnings (P/E) multiples. Mastercard has a P/E multiple of 33x, while PayPal's is 10x. In this case, PayPal stock is notably more affordable than Mastercard, giving it a leg up on this factor.

    To sum up, both of these financial stocks have their strengths. PayPal stock is quite affordable, with a valuation several times less than that of Mastercard. However, one could argue that the reason for the discount is clear: Mastercard is growing its revenue base much faster and derives far more profit from that revenue. As such, Mastercard wins this head-to-head matchup in my book.

    Nvidia’s Jensen Huang Is Back. Is the Stock a Buy?

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Many Nvidia (NVDA +31.21%) watchers and investors just got exactly what they wanted: The artificial intelligence (AI) chip giant reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive officer, president, and member of the board.
    • According to recent reports, an outpouring of support followed, including a petition to bring Huang back.
    • Industry observers note that with news of his return, the stock soared 30% within the first half hour of trading.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Adria Cimino – Nov 23, 2026 at 11:35AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Nvidia ›.

    Many Nvidia (NVDA +31.21%) watchers and investors just got exactly what they wanted: The artificial intelligence (AI) chip giant reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive officer, president, and member of the board. Huang had resigned less than two weeks ago following allegations of two affairs -- one with a person U.S. intelligence called a spy and another with an Nvidia executive.

    According to recent reports, an outpouring of support followed, including a petition to bring Huang back. Nvidia's stock had lost 24% since his resignation, extending an October decline. AI stocks in general have come under pressure periodically this year amid concerns about the depth of spending on infrastructure -- and whether it's sustainable. But the biggest drag on Nvidia stock was clearly Huang's departure.

    Industry observers note that with news of his return, the stock soared 30% within the first half hour of trading. Is this hot AI stock, which still faces certain headwinds, a buy? Let's find out.

    Jensen Huang. Image source: Nvidia.

    First, a summary of the news that led to Huang's resignation -- and his surprise return. Nvidia's board on Nov. 8 confirmed an investigation into reports that a foreign intelligence effort had targeted Huang. This followed allegations that Huang had an affair with Alice Huang (not a relative), whom U.S. intelligence called a spy. Huang, in an email to staff, apologized for being unfaithful to his wife and expressed his commitment to Nvidia and his support for the investigation.

    Days later, The Newly introduced York Times reported that Huang had a second affair, with an Nvidia employee, and Huang resigned soon afterward. The board named finance chief Colette Kress as interim CEO and started a search for a permanent leader.

    Recent findings suggest that investors worried about Nvidia's future without the leadership of Huang, seen as a visionary who has driven the company's successes and become almost the face of AI around the globe. Though Nvidia has a multi-year roadmap and contracts in place through the end of the decade, investors still questioned whether the company truly could excel without Huang at the helm. An open letter to bring Huang back garnered more than 200,000 signatures, including those of leading tech CEOs such as Elon Musk of Tesla and Space Exploration Technologies and Shopify's Tobias Lütke.

    Nvidia today confirmed the return of Huang "effective immediately." This followed a series of interviews with him, "after which the board was satisfied with respect to Mr. Huang's candor and ability to lead Nvidia." Nvidia said the decision also came after receiving "input from senior levels of the United States government." Based on this, the board considers that Huang's return doesn't represent a national security risk.

    So, is Nvidia a buy now that Huang is back? The board's investigation -- carried out by an independent committee -- into Huang's interactions with Alice Huang will continue until conclusions are reached. This remains an element of uncertainty.

    NASDAQ · As of 11:49 AM ET 11/23/26.

    However, the board's move to reinstate Huang, partially based on some input from the government, is encouraging.

    As for the company's earnings picture, it remains bright, with revenue and profit soaring in the third quarter. The release of the Vera Rubin platform has been smooth, and the company predicts 75% revenue growth for the next fiscal year based on strong visibility. Now that Huang is back, concerns about the future strategy have lifted.

    Meanwhile, the stock, even after today's explosive gains, is dirt cheap at only 17x forward earnings estimates.

    Of course, after the recent allegations involving Alice Huang, it's possible that Nvidia will come under greater government scrutiny, or that sales of chips to China may face further regulation. This could lead to some volatility or even downward pressure. Even with these challenges, though, the company's AI leadership and innovation, as well as its solid earnings track record, should make it an ongoing winner in the AI revolution. That's why, with Jensen Huang back in the driver's seat and these valuation levels, the stock is a buy -- for investors who can handle some risk and volatility.

    Mortgage Rates Today, Monday, November 23: Decidedly Higher

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1360 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nerdwallet

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Mortgage rates have had some substantial day-over-day swings lately, and today, unfortunately it's an upward swing.
    • Industry observers note that the average interest rate on a 30-year, fixed-rate mortgage jumped to 7.38% APR, according to rates provided to NerdWallet by Zillow.
    • Sources indicate that recently news about massive tech has often pulled rates down.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Mortgage rates have had some substantial day-over-day swings lately, and today, unfortunately it's an upward swing.

    Industry observers note that the average interest rate on a 30-year, fixed-rate mortgage jumped to 7.38% APR, according to rates provided to NerdWallet by Zillow. This is 14 basis points higher than yesterday and four basis points higher than a week ago. (A basis point is one one-hundredth of a percentage point.).

    Sources indicate that recently news about massive tech has often pulled rates down. Investor concerns about AI profitability keep cropping up, and when they do, tech stocks and bonds lose their appeal and Treasuries have been picking up the slack. Mortgage rates are generally benchmarked to the yield on the 10-year Treasury, and Treasury prices and yields move inversely. More demand for the 10YT drives prices up, and sends yields (and thus, mortgage rates) down.

    Today's the opposite, though. Investors are having a bout of tech exuberance as Jensen Huang got reinstated as Nvidia CEO, and lots of excitement about tech stocks and bonds means less enthusiasm for Treasuries.

    Here's the thing, though: Markets are fickle. They also move fast. And they aren't the only influence on mortgage rates.

    Here are the average APRs we're seeing today, as well as movement over the past month for context. For more, keep reading below the charts.

    » Take the next step: Compare mortgage rates from NerdWallet’s top lenders.

    According to recent reports, mortgage rates are constantly changing, since a major part of how rates are set depends on reactions to new inflation reports, job numbers, Fed meetings, global news ... you name it. For example, even tiny changes in the bond market can shift mortgage pricing.

    Industry observers note that lately, we've seen two narratives influencing mortgage rates battling it out; depending on which one's stronger, daily rates move higher or lower. Up top I talked about how shifting perceptions of big tech have been driving mortgage rates (and yes, today, pushing them higher, though usually it's pulled rates down.) When rates are moving higher, more often it's been thanks to inflation — and while it's a lightweight work week, we're about to get heavyweight inflation news.

    It has been revealed that the latest Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index is due out Wednesday. It's the Federal Reserve's preferred measure of inflation, so investors will be watching closely.

    In a recent development, the Fed doesn't set mortgage rates, but its decisions influence the entire economy. That includes mortgage lenders, who tend to adjust rates ahead of its decisions. Raising the federal funds rate (the short-term borrowing rate the central bankers actually set) is the Fed's main tactic for managing inflation, so you can guess how things are likely to go at the Fed's December meeting. Markets already feel fairly certain about a quarter-percent rate hike.

    It has been revealed that we already know how PCE's likely to go, since it's the last of the three big inflation measures to be released. We've already gotten last month's Consumer Price Index and Producer Price Index. October's CPI came in worse than predicted, showing widespread price increases. (When most of the increase is driven by one area, it's easier to be optimistic that inflation can be contained.) And October’s PPI showed wholesale inflation climbed at its fastest pace in almost four years. PPI measures the price businesses pay for things, so it's often a preview of what consumers could face once those costs get passed along.

    In a recent development, predictions for October PCE aren't great, so at this point the hope is that the numbers aren't even worse than expected. And again, PCE's out Wednesday morning. We'll know whether we're getting seconds (actually, thirds) of bad October inflation news well before the turkey hits the table on Thursday.

    And speaking of: Markets will be closed on Thanksgiving, and Black Friday's a half day, so we'll all have a bit of a break this week. Mortgage rates don't move much when the markets aren't moving. I won't be here to talk to you about mortgage rates, either, 'cause NerdWallet gives us Thursday and Friday off. Happy Thanksgiving!

Jason and Lucia would have to change a lot about their lifestyle to qualify (we know they're working on building credit, but having all your income be cash you can't really document is not going to work for a lender). But hey, I'm rooting for them.

    #142308. Why Third-Party Risk Management Is Breaking In The Era Of AI

    📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (990 w)
    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech ⚠️ Warning 🌐 Forbes ↗ Open Full Page

    Why Third-Party Risk Management Is Breaking In The Era Of AI

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (990 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Forbes

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The security industry has never quite gotten the approach to third-party risk management (TPRM) right.
    • Recent findings suggest that for as long as I can remember, TPRM has sat within the GRC function for most companies.
    • Vendors and Nth parties have emerged as one of the primary attack vectors for malicious actors.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Rami Habal, Founder & CEO, Magnitude.

    The security industry has never quite gotten the approach to third-party risk management (TPRM) right.

    Recent findings suggest that for as long as I can remember, TPRM has sat within the GRC function for most companies. For many teams, an annual questionnaire or a SOC 2 report was good enough to check the box, because vendors’ security postures would look about the same in October as they did in January.

    That world is long gone. Vendors and Nth parties have emerged as one of the primary attack vectors for malicious actors. The common thread between the most notable headlines is third-party risk that nobody was monitoring in real time. The proliferation of AI-enabled attacks is only making the problem worse. ​.

    Sources indicate that mythos surfaced more than 2,000 previously unknown software flaws in seven weeks, with subsequent reporting placing the total above 10,000. Research also projects that the median time from vulnerability discovery to a weaponized exploit could fall below one hour by the end of 2026. The traditional human-led review cycle can’t defend this expanding attack surface that’s in constant flux.

    According to recent reports, the vendor ecosystems within enterprise environments are larger and more tangled than ever before. Traditional TPRM programs were built to track direct relationships. But the risk surface now extends far beyond the vendor named in the contract.

    In a recent development, A organization might approve a customer support platform, for example, only to find that the real exposure sits several layers deeper. The platform connects to a third-party analytics tool that relies on an AI model provider, which in turn uses a cloud infrastructure partner that becomes the source of a upcoming vulnerability. None of those relationships would be visible in the original vendor review, yet any one of them can create exposure.

    Industry observers note that security teams are tracking more tools, vendors and downstream dependencies than TPRM programs were designed to manage. The problem is only getting worse as the C-suite pushes teams to deploy AI tools in the pursuit of growth and efficiency. TPRM programs weren’t built to see that far down the chain, and it’s impossible for analysts to dig into the increasingly intricate web of third and Nth parties.

    In other words, security teams are using human-paced processes to manage machine-paced environments.

    In a recent development, the annual questionnaire produces a record of assessment. A SOC 2 report provides useful evidence about controls at a moment in time. A security rating can surface signals about external posture. Each input has value, but they have a dangerous commonality: They’re all looking back in time.

    According to recent reports, none of these data points provides a continuously current view of whether a vendor, product, AI system or downstream dependency is creating exposure today. Teams cannot make decisions based on stale, outdated data and expect to protect their business from current or emerging threats.

    Industry observers note that in response to this problem, some security teams might think the best idea is to speed up the existing process, but the underlying workflow is fundamentally broken. What actually needs to change is what the third-party risk program is built to produce and measure.​.

    Industry observers note that ​Instead of treating the initial assessment as the final word on a vendor, security teams need to keep asking whether the relationship has changed as that vendor’s role and access have changed. Maybe the vendor now handles more sensitive data, supports a more critical business process or has added integrations and dependencies that were not part of the original review. Any of those changes can alter the risk profile.​.

    Vendor concentration risk is another area that is easy to miss. Several crucial vendors may rely on the same software component, AI model or infrastructure service. Looking at those vendors one at a time can make each relationship appear manageable, while the shared dependency creates a much larger exposure across the business.​.

    Teams also need to be clear about what should trigger an escalation. A fresh dependency, a major vulnerability or a change in how the business uses a vendor may signal the need for more scrutiny. Deciding in advance who owns that reassessment and what information they need can make it much easier to respond when conditions change.​.

    Sources indicate that it’s the context that surfaces from this fresh approach to TPRM that will help security teams make better decisions. In practice, that means understanding how a vendor touches the business. A payroll provider, identity platform, customer support tool and experimental AI app all create different kinds of exposure. The exact same vulnerability can introduce very different levels of risk depending on what data the third party impacted touches, what workflows they’re embedded in and your organization’s ability to keep operating if that provider is disrupted.​.

    The questions CISOs should be asking now are different than they were just a few years ago. How current is our view of our most critical vendors? What are our weakest links across our entire supply chain? What concentration risk do we have from fourth or fifth parties? Do we know where AI capabilities have entered the vendor ecosystem? Can we connect a fresh vulnerability to the exact business processes and data that may be exposed? Are GRC and security operations working from the same live picture, or are they still managing risk on separate clocks?​.

    This is where TPRM is heading. ​A function that has historically centered on point-in-time compliance reviews is transforming into a continuous security discipline. The Mythos era has accelerated that shift by introducing autonomous offensive capabilities that move faster than manual review cycles can keep pace with. Security teams need the same continuous visibility and increasingly autonomous defenses across the software supply chain.​​​.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Brendan Coffey – Updated Nov 23, 2026 at 11:41AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Intuitive Machines ›.

    Sources indicate that the race to establish a permanent presence on the moon is creating significant opportunities for space infrastructure companies. Investors are looking at Intuitive Machines (LUNR +9.46%) and Redwire (RDW +14.69%) to lead this new frontier.

    Industry observers note that intuitive Machines focuses on lunar surface access and data communication services primarily for civil government agencies. Redwire offers a broader range of hardware and autonomous systems used across national security, commercial, and scientific space missions.

    Intuitive Machines provides space infrastructure including spacecraft, lunar delivery services, and data transmission networks. It primarily serves NASA through programs like the Commercial Lunar Payload Services initiative and the Near Space Network. Customer concentration like this adds a layer of risk to the business, as NASA historically accounts for a significant majority of its revenue. Its work includes participating in the growth of the defense stock market by supporting the Space Development Agency.

    In the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached approximately $707 million, representing growth of nearly 221% compared to the prior period. This sharp increase in revenue reflects the scaling of its mission operations and recent business acquisitions. Despite this growth, the company reported a net loss of roughly $128 million for those same twelve months.

    As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the company maintained a current ratio of nearly 5.0x, which measures its ability to cover short-term liabilities with short-term assets. Its debt-to-equity ratio was approximately -0.5x. This figure indicates that total liabilities exceed shareholder equity. In the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, free cash flow was nearly negative $56.0 million, the cash remaining after the company funds its operations and capital equipment.

    According to recent reports, redwire operates as an integrated space technology tech giant that builds infrastructure and autonomous systems for a wide variety of customers. Its business is heavily weighted toward national security, which accounted for approximately 47% of its revenue in its latest annual report. The company also serves major civil agencies like NASA and the European Space Agency, while expanding its commercial footprint in satellite manufacturing. Redwire serves diverse defense clients including the U.S. Army and the U.S. Space Force.

    In the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached about $431.9 million, indicating growth of roughly 46% over the previous twelve-month period. This upward trend highlights the steady demand for its space platforms and multi-domain operations. However, the manufacturer experienced a net loss of approximately $226.1 million during this period.

    As of its December 2025 balance sheet, Redwire reported a debt-to-equity ratio of nearly 0.2x, meaning its total debt is approximately 20% of its equity. Its current ratio stood at roughly 1.6x, showing it has more current assets than current liabilities. In the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, free cash flow was approximately negative $190.8 million. Free cash flow is a measure of the actual cash a business generates after accounting for capital expenditures.

    Industry observers note that intuitive Machines faces risks related to its heavy dependence on U.S. government contracts, which can be subject to unexpected funding changes or terminations. The tech giant also requires significant capital to maintain its complex spaceflight operations and integrate the recent Lanteris acquisition. Any failure in its lunar missions could result in substantial financial losses and damage its reputation among commercial and civil partners.

    Redwire must navigate the risk that its technology could become obsolete in a rapidly changing aerospace market. In its latest annual report, the manufacturer identified material weaknesses in its internal control over financial reporting. It also faces risks from geopolitical instability affecting its European operations and must compete with larger industry players like Lockheed Martin Corp. (LMT +0.88%) and Northrop Grumman Corp. (NOC +0.95%).

    Recent findings suggest that based on the P/S ratio, Intuitive Machines right now trades at a lower valuation multiple than Redwire. The P/S ratio measures a organization's market value against its sales over the past twelve months.

    Valuation metrics include those sourced from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) and may differ from those of other data providers.

    According to recent reports, intuitive Machines has been posting superb results in fiscal 2026, most recently reporting sequential quarterly growth of 31% to $269 million in the third quarter, reported in early November. Management claims they have an order backlog of $1.9 billion, up $1.2 billion from the end of 2025. NASA is moving toward steady access-to-space flights and deliveries, too, which bodes well for the company's longer-term sales. Revenue for fiscal 2026 is expected to more than quadruple to $935 million, though net loss is expected to widen to about $100 million. Analysts expect the business to turn a profit for the first time in 2029.

    In April, Redwire was selected as one of 14 vendors (out of a total of 32 bids) on the Space Systems Command $1.8 billion 10-year Andromeda Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity, or IDIQ contract. That's a project to replace aging GPS satellites and upgrade the U.S. space infrastructure to counter emerging threats. The IDIQ win is something management feels moves Redwire up the food chain with the Department of Defense. It could mean significantly more revenue, since U.S. Space Systems Command provided a notice of its intent to raise the total shared ceiling for the Andromeda IDIQ to more than $6 billion to meet increased demand.

    In the near term, Wall Street projects Redwire to post fiscal 2026 revenue of around $463 million, representing about 38% growth over the prior year. In addition, the business has an order backlog of $620 million. The business is still expected to post net losses for the foreseeable future, but they are trending in the right direction.

    Sources indicate that these are both exciting companies contributing to the build-out of U.S. space infrastructure. Intuitive Machines' larger order backlog is appealing, offering investors a more stable pathway for the next year. At a lower price-to-sales ratio compared to Redwire, Intuitive Machines is the better choice.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, grail (GRAL +5.66%) and Guardant Health (GH +5.90%) represent two companies with significant upside potential in multi-cancer early detection (MCED) testing.
    • Here's why both are attractive for investors, and why they are a surprisingly complementary fit.
    • In a nutshell, Guardant already has an early-stage test with pre-market approval (PMA) -- Shield for colorectal cancer -- with commercial coverage and is working toward achieving a PMA for the Shield platform in multi-cancer detection (MCD).
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Lee Samaha – Nov 23, 2026 at 11:45AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Guardant Health ›.

    According to recent reports, grail (GRAL +5.66%) and Guardant Health (GH +5.90%) represent two companies with significant upside potential in multi-cancer early detection (MCED) testing. However, they differ significantly in their strategies and developmental timelines for MCED tests.

    Here's why both are attractive for investors, and why they are a surprisingly complementary fit.

    In a nutshell, Guardant already has an early-stage test with pre-market approval (PMA) -- Shield for colorectal cancer -- with commercial coverage and is working toward achieving a PMA for the Shield platform in multi-cancer detection (MCD).

    In contrast, Grail doesn't have its Galleri MCED test approved yet, or commercial or Medicare coverage yet, but it offers potential early detection of more than 50 cancers in one test.

    Recent findings suggest that as such, investing in Guardant offers investors a more secure pathway to cash flow generation (revenue grew by 36% year over year in the most recent quarter), including a tripling in Shield test volume to 83,000 as commercial coverage grows. Moreover, Guardant offers other oncology tests that act as companion diagnostics for cancer patients receiving therapy. These include tests to determine whether a cancer therapy is working effectively.

    NASDAQ · As of 11:47 AM ET 11/23/26.

    Industry observers note that these are the near-term drivers of Guardant's revenue and earnings, but over the long term the company is looking to establish Shield as a MCD test. Guardant has the advantage that the Shield platform was developed "as a multi-cancer detection platform from a single blood draw; physicians can screen for colorectal cancer and if the patient opts in, receive results for additional cancers," according to Co-CEO and founder AmirAli Talasaz.

    In other words, Shield MCD and the already-approved Shield are the same platform, meaning the lab work is the same, but Guardant still needs to be approved for other cancers.

    Sources indicate that that mentioned, a patient ordering Shield for colorectal cancer test can opt in to use Shield as an MCD, and Guardant is gathering and using that data to ultimately support a PMA submission. However, as Talasaz also notes, "we are in relatively early innings of this MCD opt-in," and Shield MCD is a profit driver one for the longer term.

    According to recent reports, in contrast, Grail's Galleri test is not one for the long term. In fact, management expects it will receive PMA from the Food and Drug Administration in early 2027. It's a critical part of the story, but not necessarily the key part. I'll explain.

    Sources indicate that grail already offers the Galleri MCED test on a self-pay basis, but it needs FDA approval to open a pathway to Medicare adoption under the Nancy Sewell Act, which allows Medicare coverage for FDA-approved MCED tests, provided the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) determines such coverage is appropriate. Grail has been in discussions with CMS for some time, and management expects it to initiate a national analysis of Galleri after the FDA grants a PMA.

    Similarly, commercial insurers are understood to be waiting for Galleri's PMA to begin discussions about providing coverage. It's a somewhat complex process at the best of times, but complicated by Galleri missing its primary endpoint (detecting cancers at an earlier stage and so reduce the incidence of late stage detection) in its landmark three-year trial with England's National Health Service (NHS).

    NASDAQ · As of 11:45 AM ET 11/23/26.

    On the other hand, the Galleri test did demonstrate more impressive data in the 12 deadly cancers that cause most cancer-related deaths in the U.S., and that's the basis of potential coverage for Galleri.

    According to recent reports, all told, Guardant offers a slower but more secure route to widespread cancer testing via Shield and Shield MCD, while Grail offers investors more near-term upside but also risk around Medicare and commercial insurer adoption, as well as uncertainty about test pricing. The difference makes them complementary stocks for an investor looking for exposure to the investment theme.

    #142298. Ground Truth: The Unsung Foundation Of Industrial Autonomy

    📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (953 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Forbes ↗ Open Full Page

    Ground Truth: The Unsung Foundation Of Industrial Autonomy

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (953 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Forbes

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Ronald Bisio is Group President, Field Systems, at Trimble.
    • ​While the public’s attention is captivated by self-driving vehicles, city robotaxis and visions of flying cars, there’s a more consequential autonomous evolution taking place across heavy industry.
    • In building and infrastructure construction, autonomy is a navigation and execution challenge.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Ronald Bisio is Group President, Field Systems, at Trimble.

    ​While the public’s attention is captivated by self-driving vehicles, city robotaxis and visions of flying cars, there’s a more consequential autonomous evolution taking place across heavy industry.

    In building and infrastructure construction, autonomy is a navigation and execution challenge. A 50-ton excavator doesn’t just travel across a construction site from Point A to Point B. It digs trenches, grades slopes and moves thousands of tons of earth to match a complex 3D digital model down to the centimeter. A commercial freight truck hauling 80,000 pounds along a highway corridor isn’t just following traffic. With advanced digital mapping and precise positioning technologies, the truck holds a precise spatial line through torrential rain, dense fog or featureless stretches of road where cameras lose contrast.

    ​In the physical world, knowing what’s immediately around a machine is critical, but a real breakthrough happens when we connect local perception through cameras, LiDAR and radar to spatial ground truth, an invisible infrastructure that complements onboard sensors. This is the high-precision global positioning that uses an absolute coordinate frame of latitude, longitude, elevation and time down to the centimeter. When we connect local perception with precise positioning, we close the gap between machinery observing what’s around and knowing exactly where the machinery sits on the physical earth.

    Industry observers note that with these technological advances in heavy industry, there’s an understandable anxiety about automation replacing human workers. But as I visit customers and jobsites, I see the opposite. Across construction and transportation, the shortage of skilled workers is evident. Contractors can’t find enough experienced workers to meet infrastructure construction demands, and fleet owners are facing historically high driver turnover.

    ​Fundamentally, industrial autonomy is about elevating human activity and decision making. By putting high-precision digital guidance into a cab, an inexperienced operator can perform complex grading work. Instead of performing repetitive manual layout, workers can oversee connected equipment, manage exceptions and focus on site safety. Autonomous equipment and robotics help automate repetitive and hazardous operations, freeing human talent to focus on higher-order tasks.

    ​Over the past few years, perception sensors have improved dramatically. Cameras, LiDAR and radar give machines exceptional eye-level vision so they can recognize nearby obstacles, workers and vehicles.

    In a recent development, ​But vision sensors have two inherent vulnerabilities. First, these optical systems may degrade in harsh environments and be rendered momentarily blind by factors like heavy dust, glare or dark tunnels. Second, vision sensors lack global context. A camera can spot an obstacle five feet away, but it can’t tell a bulldozer where it sits on the earth’s surface.​.

    Industry observers note that to address this, machines may rely on satellite positioning, but they also must be on guard for the illusion of precision. Driven by the rise of low-cost radios, increasing radio frequency interference leaves satellite signals vulnerable to both accidental jamming and deliberate spoofing. Spoofing is particularly dangerous because a legacy GPS receiver may lock onto a falsified signal and output a position with high mathematical confidence, even though the machine is actually several meters off target.

    According to recent reports, ​If a mapping app gets bad location data, a passenger vehicle driver might make a wrong turn or miss an exit. But when heavy equipment is shaping a foundation or grading a road, inaccurate location data may cause costly rework, wasted materials and safety risks.

    According to recent reports, rather than jumping straight to driverless machines on jobsites, we’re seeing a steady advancement of smart equipment guidance and operator assistance. Recent milestones in the field demonstrate the impact:​.

    Recent findings suggest that in the recent building of a fresh EV manufacturing facility, Landmark Construction, a civil contractor utilizing our positioning solutions, orchestrated more than 150 machine-guided excavators, dozers and graders connected to a single 3D digital site blueprint. Guided by continuous satellite positioning, the machines automatically adjusted blades and buckets to match design lines. By eliminating six or seven manual data transfer steps between the field and the office, earthmoving tasks that previously took a month were completed in several days—and often with more accuracy.

    It has been revealed that high-precision positioning is steadily moving out of specialized niches and into mainstream production of electric vehicles and commercial long-haul trucks. Fusing satellite data with vehicle movement sensors allows passenger cars and major trucks to maintain lane-level accuracy in urban canyons and bad weather, giving automated driver-assist systems the required reliability.

    In the air, autonomous drones are opening up new options for delivering urgent medical supplies. Guided by resilient positioning technology, these delivery drones can maintain their flight accuracy and operate safely despite localized signal degradation, bad weather and magnetic interference.

    Technology leaders considering autonomous solutions for their operations should keep these three principles in mind:.

    1. Precision is the bridge to physical reality. A few inches of spatial error may not matter in the virtual world, but on active jobsites, centimeter-level precision is what’s needed for accurate physical execution on the first pass.

    2. Spatial trust is necessary for safe autonomy. Heavy machinery can’t alter the physical world without verified, uncompromised positioning. Precision is the core safety architecture for real-world automation.

    3. Accuracy amplifies human potential. High-precision guidance elevates rather than replaces human judgment. Precision technology takes guesswork out of complex physical tasks so less experienced workers can operate like skilled veterans.

    Sources indicate that ​Industrial autonomy aims to seamlessly connect digital design and physical reality. A backbone of high-precision positioning opens up fresh possibilities for pairing intelligent machinery with human expertise. We only need to dream them into reality.

    In a recent development, forbes Technology Council is an invitation-only community for world-class CIOs, CTOs and technology executives. Do I qualify?

    Breaking: Jensen Huang Is Back as Nvidia’s CEO. Is Nvidia Stock in the Clear or Do Risks Remain?

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (853 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Nvidia's (NVDA +30.77%) board of directors shocked the world this morning by reinstating Jensen Huang as the manufacturer's CEO, president, and a member of the board.
    • Recent findings suggest that as many know, Huang resigned from Nvidia on Nov.
    • In a statement, Nvidia's board stated they felt "confident" that Huang "poses no national security risk.".
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Bram Berkowitz – Nov 23, 2026 at 11:51AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Nvidia ›.

    Nvidia's (NVDA +30.77%) board of directors shocked the world this morning by reinstating Jensen Huang as the manufacturer's CEO, president, and a member of the board.

    Recent findings suggest that as many know, Huang resigned from Nvidia on Nov. 12 following media reports that alleged Huang had multiple extramarital affairs, including one with a woman named Alice Huang (no relation), who has been accused of being a Chinese spy.

    In a statement, Nvidia's board stated they felt "confident" that Huang "poses no national security risk.".

    Recent findings suggest that "The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead NVIDIA, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers," Nvidia's board Chair Harvey Jones noted in a statement. "We have every confidence in Jensen and look forward to working with him as he resumes his leadership of the Tech giant.".

    In the statement, Huang mentioned he is "honored" to return and retakes his post "with the greatest humility and renewed commitment.".

    According to recent reports, as of 11:50 a.m. ET, Nvidia stock traded nearly 31% higher. Is the stock in the clear, or do risks remain?

    Industry observers note that jensen Huang. Image source: Nvidia.

    Sources indicate that huang is clearly a fantastic CEO from an operational perspective. He founded Nvidia 33 years ago and clearly had the foresight to see artificial intelligence coming decades before it went mainstream.

    But Huang's return may be lifting Nvidia stock for other reasons. The board stated that Huang's return poses no national security risk. Investors could interpret this to mean that Nvidia did not bypass export restrictions and sell chips that may have illegally reached China.

    According to recent reports, reports suggest that Alice Huang had set up a network to purchase chips through shell companies or companies established outside China, which then shipped them to China. If this is the case and the U.S. imposes further restrictions to prevent it, this would threaten Nvidia's future revenue and earnings, which would certainly impact the stock and the company's total value.

    The major question is how many of Nvidia's chips have been making their way to China illegally. From the outside, it's hard to believe the board would reinstate Huang if they were concerned that the company, under his direction, had knowingly bypassed export restrictions.

    NASDAQ · As of 11:45 AM ET 11/23/26.

    The reinstatement follows an interview on Nov. 22 with U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, who seemed to dial back some of his previous rhetoric directed at the company and even left the door open for Huang's return.

    In its statement, Nvidia's board said that the independent investigation it rolled out into whether Huang was the target of a foreign intelligence effort "will proceed to conclusion." The board has also created a National Security and Export Control Committee of independent directors to oversee trade compliance and national security risks.

    That feels a bit counterintuitive for the board to say it feels confident that Huang poses no national security concern, yet to continue the independent investigation. Another question is why this national security committee is only being set up now.

    Industry observers note that furthermore, the board noted on Nvidia’s recent earnings call it had no intention of reinstating Huang, so its hands may have been forced for another reason. For instance, there was strong support for Huang's reinstatement. It's possible a significant number of employees threatened to leave the organization if Huang was not reinstated. If this is the case, Nvidia's board could be acting hastily.

    Huang is also set to testify before Congress. Additionally, the U.S. Commerce Department recently imposed a rule that will prevent Chinese companies from using advanced U.S. chips that are remotely stored in data centers outside China.

    The Commerce Department will also require companies in Brazil, Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, or Thailand to obtain licenses to export or transfer chips.

    If it turns out that a material number of Nvidia's chips were purchased to be provided to Chinese companies for remote access or direct shipment, that could lead Wall Street analysts to cut their revenue and earnings projections for future years.

    Recent findings suggest that the reinstatement of Huang certainly caught me by surprise, as I didn't think it could happen so soon. I still see risks for the stock, and after the big move, the easy money has been made.

    In a recent development, nvidia isn't necessarily expensive at these levels, but I would still tread cautiously and would continue to keep future Nvidia stock purchases smaller and more speculative. I don't think this story is over.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By David Dierking – Nov 23, 2026 at 11:55AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than NASDAQ Composite Index ›.

    Industry observers note that the Nasdaq Composite (^IXIC +6.35%) fell 10% in the week ending Nov. 20, bringing its overall loss since its October high to more than 18%.

    According to recent reports, nvidia's (NVDA +31.21%) current drama and the Anthropic (ANT -2.34%) IPO are getting most of the attention. But the damage in the sector is widespread.

    Recent findings suggest that investors who went overweight in tech and artificial intelligence (AI) stocks may be wondering if the worst is over or if it's yet to come. History gives us some guidance, although it may not be as comforting as they're hoping for.

    In a recent development, before this week, the Nasdaq had dropped 10% or more in a single week exactly 10 times since 1971. The list, unfortunately, reads like a history of stock market crisis periods: Black Monday, the 2000 tech bubble, the 2008-09 Great Recession, the COVID-19 pandemic, and the "Liberation Day" tariff sell-off.

    In a recent development, each one happened during what became a bear market. The Nasdaq Composite is essentially there right now, so the current correction fits right in. The question is where the decline stops.

    Here's what the index did following those past instances of 10%-plus weekly declines:.

    In a recent development, at a high level, the results seem encouraging. The median return over the following one-month, three-month, six-month, and 12-month periods are all positive and modestly above the stock market's long-term averages.

    But the real story, I think, is the volatility.

    Across the data set, individual returns vary widely. Even in a relatively short one-month forward return, the Nasdaq Composite was down more than 11% twice but up more than 15% three times. That doesn't do much for predictability.

    Even within the same crisis period, returns were very volatile.

    It has been revealed that the key takeaway isn't that this is a consistent buy-the-dip opportunity. It's that this could be just the beginning of an extended period of above-average market volatility. And volatility tends to mean a higher risk of further declines.

    No matter what forward-looking time frame you consider, the 10% single-week decline rarely marked a low for the Nasdaq Composite. In many cases, additional declines of 10% or more were still in store.

    Recent findings suggest that plus, big drops also tended to cluster together. In seven of the 10 instances, the index suffered another weekly loss of 7% or more within the following 13 weeks. That's consistent with other studies that have shown sharp up and down moves often happen in close proximity to each other.

    In the three cases where the 10% down week occurred in close proximity to the market's bottom (September 2001, April 2000, and April 2025), the Nasdaq had already declined sharply in the lead-up.

    Sources indicate that in 2026, the Nasdaq was already about 8% to 10% below its all-time high prior to last week's 10% decline. That's not nearly as large of a correction as the market saw before the three instances mentioned above. But last week's huge decline didn't come out of the blue either.

    Sources indicate that prepare for more volatility. History shows that a 10% single-week decline usually isn't a one-off, and that additional whipsaws in stock prices can last for months.

    In a recent development, for long-term investors with 10-plus years yet to go before initiating any drawdowns, I think this is a good opportunity to either stay the course you already have planned and/or use the current drawdown to opportunistically buy the dip if you have cash for this purpose. Try to avoid making major changes to your asset allocation based on the past six weeks.

    But if you've found that the current correction has you losing sleep at night, consider adjusting to a more conservative allocation. It'll likely yield better long-term results than trying to time in and out of the market. It's best to avoid investing beyond your risk tolerance.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Tokenization platform Securitize climbed about 10% postmarket after reporting third quarter growth alongside increased operating expenses, and announcing an expansion into asset-backed finance through a strategic acquisition.

    It has been revealed that miami-based Securitize, which made its public market debut in July, operates in the relatively upcoming corner of the crypto equity universe involved in institutional tokenization infrastructure. Tokenized assets on the platform grew 9% in the third quarter, to $4.8 billion, from the same period a year ago. Aggregate transaction volume rose 20% from a year ago, to $4.3 billion. Revenue of $11.5 million was up 28% from last year.

    Recent findings suggest that the growth came as bullish sentiment around tokenization gained traction throughout the third quarter, ahead of the Security and Exchange Commission formalizing the long awaited Innovation Exemption on Sept. 17, which created a temporary pathway for trading of certain tokenized stocks and strengthened the regulatory outlook.

    Profitability is still meaningfully below year-ago levels, due in part to costs associated with going public over the summer, as well as the scaling up of the tokenization business at an active time for the entire sector, Securitize CEO Carlos Domingo told CNBC in an exclusive interview.

    Securitize reinforced "certain areas of the firm like finance, compliance, legal [and] cybersecurity," which increased corporate costs "compared to a year ago when we were privately held," Domingo said. "We're in in a very good position. The adjusted EBITDA … is improving significantly from previous quarters.".

    Securitize reported an adjusted EBITDA loss of $2 million, compared with positive adjusted EBITDA of $3.6 million a year ago, better than a $5.5 million loss in the second quarter. The organization posted a 183% increase in operating costs and expenses.

    Sources indicate that also on Monday, the Securitize board authorized a $50 million share buyback and confirmed the acquisition of River One, an institutional asset-backed financing platform developing technology to connect stablecoin capital with traditional lending markets. Terms were not disclosed.

    Securitize sees an opportunity to modernize the $9 trillion market for asset backed finance by using stablecoins to finance real world assets, generate yield and tokenize investment positions and credit products, Domingo said.The acquisition also marks an expansion beyond Securitize's core niche markets at a time when tokenization's competitive landscape is growing, with traditional asset managers like BlackRock and Franklin Templeton, and established financial market infrastructure providers like DTCC and Broadridge, entering the industry.

    "We have been very active in tokenized funds, treasuries [and] yield … And we've been obviously recently very active in tokenized stocks, so this adds another piece of the puzzle in the emerging tokenization space for us to capture revenue growth.".
