    • Recent findings suggest that A customer might love the range, performance, and design, then wonder where they'll get it serviced in a pinch.
    • Lucid is introducing another twist within its European strategy, and it's possible the move could help Lucid convince more buyers to jump on board without needing to operate more locations itself.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Daniel Miller – Nov 23, 2026 at 12:00PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Lucid Group ›.

    According to recent reports, lucid Group (LCID +6.36%) has spent plenty of time convincing investors its vehicles deserve attention. But building an impressive electric vehicle (EV) is one thing. Convincing people to pull the trigger on a major-ticket purchase can prove more challenging.

    Recent findings suggest that A customer might love the range, performance, and design, then wonder where they'll get it serviced in a pinch. Admiring a car online is easy, but signing the paperwork when support feels far away, combined with Lucid's financial uncertainty? That's a tougher sell, especially for a young EV maker such as Lucid.

    Lucid is introducing another twist within its European strategy, and it's possible the move could help Lucid convince more buyers to jump on board without needing to operate more locations itself.

    In August, Lucid named Munsterhuis Autobedrijven its first retail partner in the Netherlands. The partnership calls for a dedicated Lucid sales location in the city of Hengelo, with authorized after-sales and service at the same site. Essentially, it complements Lucid's existing Studio and Service Center in Hilversum.

    This continues a hybrid retail strategy that already included a partnership with Germany's Wackenhut. Lucid is adding independent partners alongside its own locations. The upside is worth noting for investors because an established retailer brings local relationships and experience selling and servicing cars. Lucid brings the vehicles and enjoys its expanding reach.

    For buyers, nearby sales and service could remove a reason to hesitate before making the major-ticket purchase. For shareholders, partners could provide a way to expand customer access while sharing the work of building a retail presence. All in all, it's really an underrated move by Lucid if it can expand on the idea and execute.

    It has been revealed that lucid's strategic twist isn't completely unheard of before. Chinese EV maker Nio is pursuing a related approach. In June 2025, it announced European expansion through local distribution partners, including Hedin Mobility Group for Belgium and Luxembourg.

    Industry observers note that the agreements aren't exactly identical, but the logic and strategy are similar: An automaker doesn't have to build every part of its overseas sales network from scratch. Of course, the middleman needs to make money, too. Sharing the economics with a retail partner could leave Lucid keeping less from each sale.

    But reaching more buyers while committing less capital to its own retail network could be a worthwhile trade-off for a firm trying to conserve cash.

    NASDAQ · As of 11:48 AM ET 11/23/26.

    In a recent development, the question facing investors is whether better access produces additional sales without an equally large increase in Lucid's own spending. Investors should cheer more partner appointments, broader service coverage, and evidence that the expanded network attracts customers. That said, a longer location list alone won't guarantee a spike in deliveries, demand, or revenue.

    This won't fix Lucid's business overnight, and to be fair, the young automaker has a number of problems to address. However, making its vehicles easier to buy and maintain for more potential consumers could help turn product credibility into more sales.

    In a recent development, lucid doesn't need to own every showroom. It needs more customers walking into one – and driving home in its cars.

    #142269. What's ahead for AI financing after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang departs

    📅 13 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (738 w)
    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    What's ahead for AI financing after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang departs

    📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (738 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's departure hasn't produced a broad shock to the credit market, but it is putting the organization's role as a financier of artificial intelligence infrastructure under scrutiny.
    • Huang, who stepped down Thursday amid an espionage and adultery scandal, built Nvidia into an AI powerhouse in the 33 years since he co-founded the tech giant.
    • Nvidia not only supplies its graphics processing units to hyperscalers and tech giants, it also provides financing to other companies to help the industry expand.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's departure hasn't produced a broad shock to the credit market, but it is putting the organization's role as a financier of artificial intelligence infrastructure under scrutiny.

    Huang, who stepped down Thursday amid an espionage and adultery scandal, built Nvidia into an AI powerhouse in the 33 years since he co-founded the tech giant. Chief financial officer Colette Kress has been named interim CEO as the company searches for a permanent chief executive.

    Nvidia not only supplies its graphics processing units to hyperscalers and tech giants, it also provides financing to other companies to help the industry expand. That could all change.

    "Although we expect the manufacturer to fulfill all of its previously confirmed commitments, we believe that going forward, it may be more difficult for the company to negotiate upcoming multi-party investments among ecosystem partners at the same scale it has done up to this point," Goldman Sachs analyst James Schneider noted in a note Thursday.

    The news of Huang's resignation comes after investors were already concerned about the massive amount of debt being taken on to fund AI infrastructure.

    Industry observers note that tech bond yields have risen and spreads have widened on credit default swaps, most notably in lower-rated names. Credit default swaps are contracts in which investors pay for protection in case the borrower can't repay its debt. Wider spreads indicate investors view the bonds as riskier.

    On Friday, the yield on Nvidia's 4.5% bond due in 2031 sat at 5.717%, nearly 5% higher week to date. Bond yields move inversely to prices.

    Tech stocks slumped Friday with the Nasdaq 100 closing down 1.2% as markets continued to digest the Nvidia news. Yields on hyperscaler bonds ticked slightly higher on Friday, signaling the broader concern about AI debt lingers.

    Sources indicate that it's the smaller AI companies that could ultimately see an impact if Nvidia makes any changes to its AI financing. The organization had $36 billion in off-balance-sheet AI cloud agreements, or backstops, for neoclouds, according to its last quarterly financial filing in July.

    Neoclouds CoreWeave, Nebius and IREN are all in Nvidia's portfolio. Their shares were down sharply Thursday.

    In a recent development, coreWeave, which has become the poster child for AI debt fears, saw its bond yields retreat after its quarterly earnings on Tuesday eased investor concerns. The yield on its 9.75% bond due in 2031 was 14.79% on Friday after climbing to 16.7% last week. The spread on its five-year CDS also dropped more than 17% week to date, although it remained above 1,000 — which is generally considered a sign of distress.

    It remains unclear how Nvidia's support for those companies may change, mentioned CreditSights analyst Andy Li.

    "We don't know what the ultimate strategy for Nvidia is going to be coming out the other side," he stated.

    "However, I think directionally, just given the fact that Jensen was so crucial in selling the Nvidia story and being a very aggressive deal maker, it's likely that a lot of this creative deal-making and circular financing and equity and credit support is going to moderate," he added.

    CoreWeave CEO Michael Intrator told CNBC Wednesday, before Huang's departure, that Nvidia "is not one person.".

    "There are thousands of people over there that interface with thousands of people at my company every day. They integrate on the technology. They integrate on the physical infrastructure. They integrate on the networking," he stated in an interview with "Squawk on the Street." "They have been a great partner for us for years. They will continue to be a great partner for us.".

    Bob Lang, founder and chief strategist at Explosive Options, doesn't see any significant changes in terms of Nvidia's relevance or its ability to finance for now. As CFO, Kress was involved in the financing deals, and the search for a permanent CEO is going to take some time, he noted.

    The real issue is just how much money the tech giant will want to lend for AI financing, rather than, say using its hundreds of billions in free cash flow for other purposes, like share buybacks, capex, or acquisitions.

    Sources indicate that "Substantial companies like Nvidia and Meta, they're holding all the cards," he noted. "When they decide that the game is over, that's it — it's going to be curtains for some of these smaller companies.".

    — CNBC'S Kif Leswing and Isabel O'Brien contributed reporting.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The Boston Celtics, thanks to a major defensive stand from Draymond Green late, are now on their worst losing skid in years.
    • Industry observers note that the Celtics fell to the Golden State Warriors 88-87 on Sunday night at the Chase Center in San Francisco.
    • According to recent reports, it had gone a ridiculous 429 games without a four-game losing skid, which was the second-longest stretch in franchise history.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Boston Celtics, thanks to a major defensive stand from Draymond Green late, are now on their worst losing skid in years.

    Industry observers note that the Celtics fell to the Golden State Warriors 88-87 on Sunday night at the Chase Center in San Francisco. That was Boston's fourth straight loss, which marked the first time the franchise had lost four consecutive games since May 2021.

    According to recent reports, it had gone a ridiculous 429 games without a four-game losing skid, which was the second-longest stretch in franchise history. The Celtics once went 468 games from 1962-68.

    Boston led by as many as 11 late in the third quarter, and seemed in a great spot to grab the win. But the Warriors chipped away and got back into the game, and even took the lead on a Brandin Podziemski 3-pointer with about 2:30 left in the contest. Those were the last points the Warriors scored.

    With just eight seconds left, Tatum had a great look to win the game. Down by a point, Tatum drove at Green and took a fadeaway jumper from the elbow. The shot was off the mark, and he finished going 0 of 7 from the field in the second half.

    Podziemski led the Warriors with 18 points and seven rebounds in the win, which moved them to 9-8 on the season and ended a five-game losing streak of their own. Charles Bassey added 13 points and nine rebounds, and Green finished with nine points. The Warriors are still missing Stephen Curry, who is sidelined with an abdominal injury.

    Tatum finished with 27 points and 10 rebounds while shooting 8 of 20 from the field. Derrick White had 14 points, and Luka Garza added 10 off the bench. They were the only three Celtics to hit double figures, and the 87 points they managed as a team were the fewest they've scored all season.

    The Celtics had double-digit leads in three of their four losses, including a 17-point lead over the Denver Nuggets before blowing that contest Wednesday. They were up by 13 points at Sacramento on Saturday before Keegan Murray sank a put-back jumper to seal the one-point win.

    Boston got the losing streak started Monday in a 10-point loss to the Orlando Magic, who rallied late to grab the win at TD Garden.

    Sources indicate that boston sits at 11-6 on the season. In spite of the losing streak, that's still good for third in the Eastern Conference standings, behind only the Philadelphia 76ers and Atlanta Hawks.

    Industry observers note that but their run of keeping losing streaks to a minimum has ended. They'll have a chance to snap the four-game losing skid Tuesday night against the Washington Wizards.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton warned Americans to prepare for "bumps in the road" after a set of damaging technology outages rocked air travel and systems like Microsoft Outlook.
    • Government officials have largely dismissed the prospects that the outages, which also slowed bank transactions, are linked to a coordinated or artificial intelligence cyberattack.
    • Clayton, however, said on CNN's "State of the Union" that outages may continue as companies and the government upgrade their systems to adapt to the AI age.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton warned Americans to prepare for "bumps in the road" after a set of damaging technology outages rocked air travel and systems like Microsoft Outlook.

    Government officials have largely dismissed the prospects that the outages, which also slowed bank transactions, are linked to a coordinated or artificial intelligence cyberattack.

    Clayton, however, said on CNN's "State of the Union" that outages may continue as companies and the government upgrade their systems to adapt to the AI age.

    "The American people should be prepared for a great deal of investment in upgrading our systems; they should be prepared for investment in cybersecurity, and they should be prepared that any time there is a step change in technology, a step change in both compute and applications, there will be bumps in the road," Clayton said.

    "You prepare by knowing that systems are going to be upgraded; they may be interrupted for a period of time and that companies and government are dealing with this on the front foot," he remarked.

    Clayton's warning came as the U.S. prepares to celebrate Thanksgiving on Thursday, one of the busiest travel weeks of the year. A technology outage prompted a nationwide ground stop just over a week ago, which lasted for hours.

    The Federal Aviation Administration noted router upgrades caused a flood of data that led to the ground stop, and that there is no indication of a cyberattack.

    Separately, Microsoft said the Outlook outage was caused by "an matter during an earlier network capacity upgrade.".

    Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent delivered a similar message on CBS' "Face the Nation.".

    Asked if Americans should be concerned about the security of their financial institutions, Bessent said: "No, they shouldn't.".

    "The patches may cause a glitch," he said, referring to measures banks are taking to safeguard from AI. "I think the American people should think of it as a vaccine; your arm may hurt, you may feel a little bad the next day, but it increases your long-term immunity and resiliency.".

    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Yahoo ↗ Open Full Page

    Bengals-Commanders Monday Night Football betting odds, picks and predictions: Best bets, player props

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1304 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Yahoo

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The top of the betting market's power ratings is like a hot nightclub.
    • The gatekeepers have something of a one-in, one-out policy, where there's only room for so many.
    • After nine weeks of the NFL season, there were four teams considered a cut above:.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The top of the betting market's power ratings is like a hot nightclub.

    The gatekeepers have something of a one-in, one-out policy, where there's only room for so many. But … if you're playing well enough, the limits will be pushed, and we'll find room for you.

    After nine weeks of the NFL season, there were four teams considered a cut above:.

    Due to mediocre results, preseason lounge regulars — the Rams and Seahawks — have been left out in the coat room, while the Chiefs are always lingering in the front bar.

    Then Joe Burrow and his crew demonstrated up, blazing with a five-game winning streak, and an utter destruction of a division rival on prime time in Week 10.

    The Bengals got their invite past the velvet rope, but now it's up to them to behave so as not to get bounced back out.

    A week ago, the lookahead line for this matchup was Bengals -3.5, so there's a very easy measurement as to literally how much has changed after one game, since the Commanders' own Thursday Night Football win shouldn't have hurt the already-modest perception of Washington — three full points.

    The Bengals offense has put up 30+ points in each of its last five games, but with a predominantly passing-centric offense, let's take a look at the pass defense metrics of their opponents, by Success Rate (adjusted for garbage time and high-leverage plays like turnovers and fourth downs):.

    After a season where the Commanders defense was a legitimate liability, they've quietly shown improvement, not allowing 30 points since Week 3, and the opponent Success Rate on dropbacks against Washington is 43.6% (seventh in the NFL).

    One of those games was against fellow club member, and offensive equal, San Francisco, which carried a similar point spread of 49ers -6.5 in Week 6, but that was at home, and the Commanders got inside the number and then almost took the lead late.

    The unfortunate part about getting into the betting market's VIP room, is that you're asked to perform at a high level to cash tickets for your bettors.

    The Bills barely scraped over the 16.5 points required of them, while the Bears couldn't cover the 11.5-point spread they were favored by over the Saints, and the Jaguars were exposed by the Giants — the first functional team they've played in weeks. Of course, the 49ers (constants in the "club" by covering spreads at a high power rating) continued to prove they belong, crushing the Vikings 35-10 on Sunday night.

    Industry observers note that the other issue the Bengals' recent victims have had is that their offense had little chance of keeping up, even if they could slow Burrow in the passing game. Quarterbacks Tyler Huntley, Malik Willis, Cam Ward, Michael Penix Jr. and (advanced-age) Aaron Rodgers don't have the efficiency or second receiving threat that Jayden Daniels has.

    Since returning from his early-season injury in Week 5, Daniels and the Commanders have an adjusted EPA/Play just behind the Cowboys and Broncos — and ahead of the Lions.

    At home, still in divisional contention and on Monday night, look for this to be closer than you might think having seen Cincinnati in action last Sunday night.

    Bet: Commanders +6.5 (-114, Bet365).

    Chase Brown under 46.5 rushing yards (-115, Bet365).

    According to recent reports, brown is like a closer who is there to throw a changeup, like the Trevor Hoffman of running backs. However, if Cincinnati doesn't face the short-yardage situations it might have against the lesser defenses they've played of late, or have a massive halftime lead, Brown's usage or efficiency might come down.

    During the five-game winning streak, Brown topped out at 57 (with 36 yards on three carries in one second-half drive) and 55 yards (thanks to a meaningless, end-of-regulation carry for eight yards).

    Tee Higgins over 5.5 receptions (+108, DraftKings).

    According to recent reports, the Commanders have struggled keeping the ball out of the hands of No. 1 receivers, as CeeDee Lamb, Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Puka Nacua combined for 32 receptions against Washington.

    That might be a general point of emphasis for Dan Quinn, facing Ja'Marr Chase on Monday, but the problem is the Bengals have two top-tier wide receivers.

    Recent findings suggest that tee Higgins' yardage totals have tailed off recently as Chase has had his way, but even as the second option, Higgins has five catches on six targets in a pair of blowouts. With a closer game, and more looks, he should get back to hauling in the 6+ catches he had in four of five before that.

    Jayden Daniels over 223.5 passing yards (-113, FanDuel).

    Whether it's as part of staying connected with the Bengals on the scoreboard, or trailing, if the game does start the way others have for Cincinnati opponents, Daniels should be spreading the ball around through the air.

    Daniels has gone over this total in three of his last four games, with the other coming in a game with a division rival, the Eagles, where Philadelphia's offense didn't provide any kind of pressure to air it out.

    CINCINNATI, OHIO - NOVEMBER 15: Tee Higgins #5 of the Cincinnati Bengals runs out of bounds during an NFL football game against the Pittsburgh Steelers at Paycor Stadium on November 15, 2026 in Cincinnati, Ohio.

    Higgins was also held out of the end zone last week, after a run of five touchdowns in three previous games.

    On his way to a third-straight 10+ touchdown season, scoring more often than not as long as Burrow is in the lineup, we'll take Higgins at around even-money.

    TE Mike Gesicki (+190, DraftKings).

    Only the Lions allow more production (yardage and touchdowns) to opposing tight ends than the Commanders, and if there was one throw that Burrow would have liked to have back during an exquisite prime-time performance, it's the one he air-mailed by about 18 inches to Mike Gesicki in the back of the end zone. After five straight games with a score, back-to-back without one feels like a drought, but we know Gesicki will get a look or two.

    RB Jacory Croskey-Merritt (+135, Bet365).

    The Commanders also get their No. 1 runner back on Monday, and maybe, David Blough will shift away from his the torturous goal-line play-calling we were subjected to against the Giants, with a tailback he's more comfortable handing the ball to in those situations?

    Jacory Croskey-Merritt is coming off IR for the first time since an 11-carry, 82-yard performance, with a touchdown in Week 5, so we'll assume he's getting the primary role back.

    In his rookie season, "Bill" had eight rushing touchdowns, so that's 10 in 22 career games.

    TE Chigoziem Okonkwo (+240, FanDuel).

    No team has allowed more yards per catch to the tight end position than the Bengals, and (eventually) that translated to a Pat Freiermuth touchdown last week. With four explosive catches, that's one shy of the team lead for Washington, so this might be as good an opportunity as Okonkwo has had all season to get his first touchdown.

    WR Treylon Burks (+310, Bet365).

    The ball was briefly in Burks' hands at the end of the aforementioned game with the 49ers, but he hasn't scored since getting in the end zone in two of his first three games this season.

    Burks' size (6-foot-2, 225 pounds) makes him a different type of option in the red zone, compared to the other receivers — Stefon Diggs and Antonio Williams — who are under six feet and less than 200 lbs.

    Not scoring recently lengthens Burks' odds, while a high game total suggests anyone is a little more likely to score than usual, creating value on a longer shot.

    You can find more valuable betting analysis from Yahoo Sports betting contributor, Matt Russell, at THE WINDOW.

    #142254. Latest Update: French biotech rejects short seller’s cancer-risk claims after shares plunge 17%

    📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (384 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚠️ Warning 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Latest Update: French biotech rejects short seller’s cancer-risk claims after shares plunge 17%

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (384 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • French biotech Abivax's stock has partially recovered after the organization responded to short seller Scorpion Capital accusing it of serious scientific and safety shortcomings in its experimental inflammatory bowel disease drug, obefazimod.
    • In a report published Friday, Scorpion alleged that Abivax's laboratory-commissioned tests indicated obefazimod may act through nonspecific toxic effects on cells, rather than the targeted biological mechanism the company described.
    • After the closing bell, Abivax said Scorpion's report contained "numerous factually inaccurate and misleading statements, assumptions, and conclusions.".
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    French biotech Abivax's stock has partially recovered after the organization responded to short seller Scorpion Capital accusing it of serious scientific and safety shortcomings in its experimental inflammatory bowel disease drug, obefazimod.

    In a report published Friday, Scorpion alleged that Abivax's laboratory-commissioned tests indicated obefazimod may act through nonspecific toxic effects on cells, rather than the targeted biological mechanism the company described. Abivax's Paris-listed shares fell 17%.

    After the closing bell, Abivax said Scorpion's report contained "numerous factually inaccurate and misleading statements, assumptions, and conclusions.".

    Shares rose 10% in Monday morning trading.

    Recent findings suggest that obefazimod is Abivax's only drug. It has shown benefits for patients with ulcerative colitis in a late-stage trial. Abivax has noted it aims to file for FDA approval by the end of the year, with a potential U.S. launch in 2027.

    Obefazimod is also being tested for Crohn's disease, another inflammatory bowel disease, in a mid-stage trial.

    Analysts have hailed the drug's potential as a best-in-class treatment for ulcerative colitis patients through its novel way of affecting multiple inflammatory pathways, as well as its potential multi-billion-dollar addressable market.

    Scorpion Capital alleged that obefazimod may not work through the mechanism claimed by Abivax, but instead act as a nonspecific agent that could damage cells.

    It also noted its laboratory testing raised concerns about catalytic phototoxicity — where a light-absorbing molecule absorbs light energy and triggers potentially damaging chemical reactions — and alleged a possible connection to skin cancer cases reported in Abivax's phase 3 trials.

    Scorpion also questioned the reliability of scientific research underpinning the treatment and suggested that its chemical properties could contribute to skin cancer risks.

    It has been revealed that in June, investors were spooked as cancer cases were reported in the study cohort in a late-stage trial of obefazimod in patients with ulcerative colitis. In a part-two dataset from the same trial, Abivax noted malignancies were in line with expected rates, helping shares recover losses.

    CEO Marc de Garidel has previously told CNBC that the medicine has "unmatched efficacy for the drug in a hard-to-treat population" and repeated the company's stance that it is safe.

    "When you have ulcerative colitis, unfortunately, your immune system is depleted, and you are more susceptible to a certain type of cancer," he said in July.

    #142246. Is a bottom in for the Nasdaq-100? Charts to watch

    📅 13 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (580 w)
    📖 Baca
    Gadgets ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Is a bottom in for the Nasdaq-100? Charts to watch

    📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (580 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • (See the video above for Frank's complete chart breakdown.).
    • Is the Nasdaq-100's recent bounce a sign that the bottom is in?
    • In a recent development, first, let's remember how we got here.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    (See the video above for Frank's complete chart breakdown.).

    Is the Nasdaq-100's recent bounce a sign that the bottom is in? We're going to look at several charts to help answer that question.

    In a recent development, first, let's remember how we got here. In September, the NDX broke out from a bullish cup-and-handle pattern, producing a 33,200-upside target. That breakout quickly failed, however, and gave way to a bearish pattern that broke down aggressively two weeks ago.

    The decline brought the index relatively close to its 26,350 downside target before the current rebound began.

    Sources indicate that zooming out, it's telling to see where the bounce originated. Three important forms of support converged in the 25,000-26,000 area:.

    This confluence of support helped encourage buying after a roughly 15% decline.

    For perspective, we also see what larger drawdowns of 20%, 30%, 40%, and 50% would look like … a lot worse.

    The following chart tracks NDX drawdowns from 52-week highs going back to just after the financial crisis. Only a handful of declines exceeded 20%, and three produced relatively quick reversals: late 2018, the Covid lows in 2020 and April 2025.

    Historically, buying into declines of approximately 15%–25% has generally paid off, even when additional downside occurred first (yellow highlights).

    The chart also highlights previous declines of 10%–16% in green, putting the current pullback into perspective.

    Industry observers note that the major exception was 2022, when the NDX eventually declined nearly 36% over approximately 10 months ... a much worse outcome, which many investors are concerned could happen again now.

    That raises the key question: Are we experiencing another routine correction, or the early stages of a larger bear market?

    One important clue will be how far this bounce progresses.

    Industry observers note that any rally that fails to reclaim the previous highs could establish a significant lower high. Additional lower highs would provide stronger evidence of a developing, longer downtrend.

    We saw this in March 2022, when that first sharp rebound effort failed to reach the previous high before a much more severe decline followed.

    The bottom line: The current bounce is encouraging, particularly given where it originated and knowing how well buying prior 10-20% drawdowns has paid off.

    From here, it's all about the follow through. We don't need to see upcoming highs right away, but any rally from here that's met with another wave of strong selling could reignite downside momentum.

    #142244. Tech outages are fueling a latest doomsday economy

    📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1308 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Tech outages are fueling a latest doomsday economy

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1308 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, A spate of high-profile technology outages that grounded planes, halted email access and slowed bank transactions have left many people worried about artificial intelligence-driven cyberattacks and the state of the U.S.
    • Sources indicate that government officials have dismissed rumors and speculation circulating online that there could be a nefarious culprit for the series of malfunctions.
    • In recent days, the Houston resident has purchased propane and lighter fluid for cooking and heating equipment that can be used without electricity.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Americans are shopping like there's no tomorrow.

    In a recent development, A spate of high-profile technology outages that grounded planes, halted email access and slowed bank transactions have left many people worried about artificial intelligence-driven cyberattacks and the state of the U.S. energy grid.

    Sources indicate that government officials have dismissed rumors and speculation circulating online that there could be a nefarious culprit for the series of malfunctions. Despite those assurances, consumers like Sabrina Cepeda are readying for a larger-scale technology blackout or other emergency event.

    In recent days, the Houston resident has purchased propane and lighter fluid for cooking and heating equipment that can be used without electricity. The mother of three also replenished her backup stockpiles of non-perishable foods, hygiene products and allergy medicine in the event that her family is homebound for several days.

    It has been revealed that "I have a way to keep my family fed, clean, hydrated, warm and safe," mentioned Cepeda, 39. "You want to have these things and not need them, rather than need them and not have them.".

    According to recent reports, the doomsday economy is catching a bid. Wall Street and retailers are taking note.

    According to recent reports, at least half a dozen major technology outages took place in the U.S. between Nov. 12 and Nov. 17. In that time frame, spending at brands specializing in emergency products spiked about 400% compared with the same period a year prior, according to card data analyzed exclusively for CNBC by Consumer Edge.

    At Ready America, which sells products like emergency survival kits, prepackaged water and high-calorie food bars, sales through e-commerce platforms have seen a roughly five-fold increase in recent days. In addition, corporate customers who keep the Vista, California-based organization's supplies in their offices in case of emergency have called in to order more.

    Sources indicate that the company has rarely seen this much demand since the Covid pandemic sent Americans into lockdown more than six years ago, said Ready America President Trevyn Reese. As a result, Ready America asked its suppliers to scale up production. The family-owned business has faced a shortage of water purification tablets, and redirected shoppers to alternative offerings like prepackaged water pouches.

    "With everything going on in the news right now, we've seen a large spike of people wanting to get prepared," said Reese.

    While the string of outages brought power-related concerns to a boiling point, data indicates that worries had been bubbling under the surface for weeks.

    Shoppers began significantly ramping up buying from emergency preparedness brands late last month, according to Consumer Edge. Around that time, Fox News reported that the Pentagon was preparing U.S. military bases to operate for at least 90 days without external support. Exacerbating those fears was the ongoing war with Iran that President Donald Trump signaled could ramp back up.

    Industry observers note that firearm trade group NSSF stated that gun sales rose about 8% in October from the same month a year prior. Retailers and gun manufacturers have anecdotally reported that demand has remained elevated into November, which NSSF said can be attributed to a combination of uncertainty tied to the midterm election and the recent outages.

    "If people are investing in firearms and ammunition, they're telling you very directly, with their wallet, what their priority is," stated Mark Oliva, NSSF's managing director of public affairs. "You're literally investing in a product that's going to be able to protect your life and protect the lives of your family.".

    Now, the doomsday talk has begun making its way to Wall Street.

    Sources indicate that mizuho told clients on Monday that consumer worries about the outages — coupled with what the bank called "apocalyptic concerns" swirling on social media — drove shoppers to stock up on emergency supplies at Costco. As a result, Mizuho stated it expects a key measure of non-fuel sales growth for Costco in November to rise above 10% for the first time since 2022.

    And RBC said so-called doomsday prepping has had a "real impact" on buying behavior around the globe over recent weeks. Still, the Canadian bank reported that the trend has so far boosted sales for only a small basket of items, such as shelf-stable proteins, water purification products and dry-pantry foods.

    Clients of Richard McWhorter, a private wealth advisor at SRM, have been rushing to Costco to buy goods in bulk and splurging for power generators. McWhorter mentioned he's also fielded questions about how to prepare for a situation in which the financial system goes down.

    "I've never seen anything like this in my life," McWhorter noted. "There's the financial side of what I do, and then there's the psychological side. And the past two weeks have been much more psychological.".

    Metal dealer American Hartford Gold reported an uptick in customer inquiries this week. Company president Max Baecker mentioned he heard from some customers that their interest in products like gold — long considered a safe-haven asset during times of turmoil — was driven by newfound concern about being overly reliant on digital financial networks following a glitch at JPMorgan Chase that affected customer transactions for several hours.

    Vice President JD Vance abruptly canceled his appearance at a Latest York Times summit on Wednesday to attend meetings about the technology outages. A day prior, Jay Clayton, the U.S. director of national intelligence, told CNBC that the recent outages were not a cyberattack or a coordinated effort by a foreign nation.

    Still, Sen. Mark Warner, D-Va., told CNBC on Wednesday that people were "freaked out" by the outages. Warner, who acts as the vice chairman of the Senate Intelligence Committee, said that the U.S. was "lucky" to have not yet seen a major AI-generated cyberattack or crisis due to AI agents going rogue.

    Investors may begin pushing companies to accelerate their cybersecurity spending out of an abundance of caution around rogue AI agents following the outages, according to Macro Hive CEO Bilal Hafeez. Such a situation would be reminiscent of the antivirus software push seen during the dot-com boom, he remarked.

    Industry observers note that the Global X Cybersecurity ETF (BUG) has climbed around 3% over the past two weeks, bucking the downtrend seen among AI stocks and the broader technology trade. The Nasdaq Composite on Friday fell into negative territory for 2026, putting the tech-heavy index on track for its first losing year since 2022.

    Industry observers note that to be sure, not everyone on social media has bought into the idea that they should be prepping for a doomsday scenario. In satirical videos posted on TikTok, users joked that they were gearing up by placing orders in the Starbucks drive-thru or purchasing significant quantities of alcohol.

    Still, the topic appears to be on the minds of a growing number of Americans. U.S. Google searches for the term "prepping" have more than doubled when comparing the past month with the same period a year prior. On YouTube, queries for videos about "survivalism," a term describing the practice of preparing for emergencies, have soared by more than 5,000% over the same time frame.

    It has been revealed that cepeda, the Houston mom, sees emergency prep efforts as a way to be safe rather than sorry. She's previously tapped into backup food stashes during extreme weather events like Hurricane Harvey in 2017 and Winter Storm Uri in 2021.

    But this year is the first time that she's felt she needed to be prepared for a potential emergency caused by technology outages, she mentioned. Cepeda and her husband have ensured they have enough cash on hand and fuel in their cars if there's a broader hit to the U.S. power grid, she said.

    In a recent development, "We rely so much on technology," Cepeda noted. "You need to be able to do these things the more traditional, old-fashioned way.".

    Retirees face a looming deadline for required withdrawals — missing it could trigger a tax penalty

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that every year, millions of Americans must take required withdrawals from retirement accounts by Dec. 31.

    Amid the busy holiday season, it's easy to miss the year-end deadline for required minimum distributions — a mistake that can trigger a hefty IRS penalty, experts said.

    "One of the most common RMD mistakes is waiting until the last minute," stated certified financial planner Alex Canellopoulos, director of wealth at Vista Capital Partners in Portland, Oregon.

    Industry observers note that most retirees must start RMDs from pretax accounts at age 73. The withdrawal is based on the previous year's account balances on Dec. 31, your age and an IRS "life expectancy factor.".

    Recent findings suggest that the first annual RMD deadline is April 1 of the year after you turn 73, and future withdrawals are due by Dec. 31. If you wait until April 1 for the first one, you'll need two RMDs that year.

    RMDs also apply to certain inherited IRAs if the original IRA owner reached RMD age before their death.

    Industry observers note that in 2023, more than 14.8 million taxpayers age 70 or older had a traditional individual retirement account, according to the latest IRS data. The average year-end market value of the accounts was about $330,000.

    Deferring RMDs until the last minute raises the likelihood of mistakes, such as overlooking certain retirement accounts or making withdrawal calculation errors, Canellopoulos noted.

    Some 7% of Vanguard investors at RMD age missed their yearly withdrawal in 2025, up slightly from 6.7% in 2024, according to a Vanguard analysis of about 400,000 RMD-age retirees with IRA balances published in December 2025.

    Among those investors, the average missed RMD was $10,500 in 2025, Vanguard told CNBC.

    Sources indicate that investors who don't take RMDs by the annual deadline may owe an excise tax to the IRS, worth up to 25% of the amount they should have withdrawn. For example, the excise tax could be up to $2,625 for a $10,500 missed RMD.

    If investors miss a required withdrawal, they could reduce the penalty to 10% if they "timely corrected" the RMD within two years and file Form 5329, according to the IRS.

    Sources indicate that in some cases, the IRS could waive the penalty entirely due to "reasonable error" if investors take "reasonable steps" to fix the shortfall, according to the agency. Investors can file Form 5329 with a letter of explanation to request the waiver.

    "If you don't ask, you're not going to get it," stated certified public accountant Tim Steffen, director of advanced planning at financial services firm Baird. "I've never heard of anybody being denied the waiver.".

    Investors who give to charity may be skipping a specific donation strategy that can reduce or eliminate their annual RMDs, according to Lawrence Pon, a CFP and CPA based in Redwood City, California.

    They can use a so-called qualified charitable distribution, or QCD, Pon stated.

    A QCD has a dual tax benefit: It doesn't count as taxable income and may also satisfy at least part of an investor's yearly RMD, Pon said.

    The move requires a direct transfer from an investor's pretax IRA to an eligible nonprofit organization. They can donate up to $111,000 in 2026. While QCD eligibility begins at age 70½, transfers won't start counting toward RMDs until an investor reaches their RMD age.

    According to recent reports, generally, taxpayers only get a tax break for large charitable donations if they itemize deductions on their tax returns. But QCDs still provide a tax benefit for charitable gifts when investors use the standard deduction.

    QCDs "provide a real benefit if you are not itemizing [tax deductions]," mentioned Pon.

    Recent findings suggest that while there's no tax deduction for QCDs, the transfer won't increase a taxpayer's adjusted gross income, or AGI. Raising AGI can cause other tax consequences, such as higher premiums for Medicare Part B and Part D.
